Yn y fersiwn ddwyieithog, mae’r golofn chwith yn cynnwys yr iaith a lefarwyd yn y cyfarfod. Mae’r golofn dde yn cynnwys cyfieithiad o’r areithiau hynny.

Mae [R] yn dynodi bod yr Aelod wedi datgan buddiant wrth gyflwyno’r busnes.

In the bilingual version, the left-hand column includes the language used during the meeting. The right-hand column includes a translation of those speeches.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cyfarfu'r Senedd yn y Siambr a thrwy gynhadledd fideo am 13:30 gyda'r Dirprwy Lywydd (Kerry Ferguson) yn y Gadair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: Datganiad gan y Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: Statement by the Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prynhawn da. Cyn symud at yr eitem gyntaf, mae'n fraint gennyf gyhoeddi canlyniad y balot cyntaf ar gyfer Bil Aelod yn y seithfed Senedd, a gynhaliwyd heddiw. Mae'n bleser gennyf gyhoeddi mai'r tri Aelod a ddewiswyd yn y balot heddiw yw James Evans, Sam Rowlands a Llŷr Powell. Llongyfarchiadau mawr i chi i gyd. Edrychaf ymlaen at weld yr hyn y byddwch chi'n ei gynnig maes o law, a dyma ddymuno'n dda i chi wrth i'r gwaith fynd rhagddo.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Good afternoon. Before we move to our first item, it's my pleasure to announce the result of the first Member Bill ballot for the seventh Senedd, which was held today. I'm pleased to announce that the three Members selected in today's ballot are James Evans, Sam Rowlands and Llŷr Powell. Congratulations to you all. I look forward in time to seeing the proposals that you bring forward and wish you all well as the work proceeds.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Item 1 on our agenda today is questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport. Question 1, Tom Montgomery.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Gwasanaethau Llyfrgell
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Library Services

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gefnogi'r gwaith o ehangu gwasanaethau llyfrgell yng Nghlwyd? OQ64690
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What steps is the Welsh Government taking to support the expansion of library services in Clwyd? OQ64690

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae gan awdurdodau lleol gyfrifoldeb statudol i ddarparu gwasanaeth llyfrgell cynhwysfawr ac effeithlon. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi llyfrgelloedd yng Nghlwyd drwy gyllid cyfalaf a refeniw. Yn 2026-27, mae hyn yn cynnwys dyfarnu £349,000 i ariannu gwelliannau cyfalaf yn llyfrgell Bae Colwyn a llyfrgell y Rhyl. Mae llyfrgelloedd ledled Clwyd hefyd wedi elwa eleni o dros £50,000 o gyllid ar gyfer prosiectau llai.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Local authorities have a statutory responsibility to provide a comprehensive and efficient library service. The Welsh Government supports libraries in Clwyd through capital and revenue funding. In 2026-27, this includes awarding £349,000 to fund capital improvements in Colwyn Bay library and Rhyl library. Libraries across Clwyd have also benefited this year from over £50,000 of funding for smaller projects.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Minister. A local authority in Clwyd in 2023 resolved to reduce library one-stop shop opening hours by 40 per cent. This was despite over 4,500 residents responding to the consultation—the most that the local authority had seen in years. Ninety per cent of those responses warned that the closure or reduction in hours would limit their ability to visit their local library, and 96 per cent of these submissions submitted negative comments about the proposal. The local authority went ahead because its hands, to a certain extent, were tied financially by the funding formula. The significant change has seen around £360,000 saved but severely limits residents' access to this important service. So, what steps are you taking to support local library services, and what discussions have you had with the Minister for local government on seeing a funding formula that specifically protects library services? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Yn 2023, penderfynodd awdurdod lleol yng Nghlwyd leihau oriau agor siop un stop llyfrgelloedd 40 y cant. Roedd hyn er bod dros 4,500 o drigolion wedi ymateb i'r ymgynghoriad—y mwyaf roedd yr awdurdod lleol wedi'i weld ers blynyddoedd. Rhybuddiodd 90 y cant o'r ymatebion hynny y byddai cau llyfrgell neu leihau oriau yn cyfyngu ar eu gallu i ymweld â'u llyfrgell leol, a chyflwynodd 96 y cant o'r cyflwyniadau hyn sylwadau negyddol am y cynnig. Bwriodd yr awdurdod lleol ymlaen â'r cynlluniau gan fod eu dwylo ynghlwm yn ariannol, i ryw raddau, oherwydd y fformiwla gyllido. Mae'r newid sylweddol wedi arwain at arbed oddeutu £360,000 ond mae'n cyfyngu'n ddifrifol ar fynediad trigolion at y gwasanaeth pwysig hwn. Felly, pa gamau rydych chi'n eu cymryd i gefnogi gwasanaethau llyfrgell lleol, a pha drafodaethau rydych chi wedi'u cael gyda'r Gweinidog llywodraeth leol ynglŷn â chyflwyno fformiwla gyllido sy'n diogelu gwasanaethau llyfrgell yn benodol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae'r Aelod yn codi mater o bwys, dwi'n gwybod, i nifer o'n hetholwyr ni ledled Cymru. Dwi'n cydnabod yr heriau y mae awdurdodau lleol wedi eu hwynebu oherwydd setliad ariannol y blynyddoedd diwethaf yma a'r effaith y mae hynny wedi ei chael ar lyfrgelloedd lleol yn benodol. Un o'r pethau rydyn ni'n ei wneud fel rhan o'r gwaith o ddatblygu'r strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon newydd ydy edrych ar wasanaethau lleol. Dwi wedi cael trafodaethau eisoes gyda rhai o arweinyddion llywodraeth leol yng Nghymru, a Chymdeithas Llywodraeth Leol Cymru, er mwyn gwir ddeall pa mor fregus ydy rhai o'r gwasanaethau hyn.

Yn ganolog i'n strategaeth newydd ni mae sicrhau mynediad cyfartal i bawb. Felly, rydyn ni eisiau deall beth ydy'r heriau sydd wedi bod yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf yma, beth mae hynny wedi ei olygu i wasanaethau o ran llyfrgelloedd ledled Cymru. Rhan fawr o'r gwaith nesaf wedyn fydd edrych ar y strategaeth hirdymor yna o ran beth ydy gwasanaeth llyfrgelloedd sy'n gweithio i'n cymunedau ni, gan gydnabod nad ydy'r gwasanaeth yn cyrraedd y nod ym mhob rhan o Gymru ar y funud.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
The Member raises an important issue, I know, for many of our constituents across Wales. I do acknowledge the challenges that local authorities have faced because of the financial settlements of these past years and the impact that that has had on local libraries in particular. One of the things that we are doing as part of our work in developing the culture and sports strategy is looking at local services. I have had discussions already with some local government leaders in Wales and the Welsh Local Government Association, in order to try and truly understand how fragile some of these services are.

Central to our new strategy is ensuring equal access for everyone. So, we want to understand what these challenges have been over past years, what that has meant to services in terms of libraries across Wales. A large part of our next piece of work will involve looking at that long-term strategy in terms of what library services that work for our communities look like, recognising that the service doesn't always meet our ambition in all parts of Wales at the moment.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Libraries are essential services for young and old, often going far past the borrowing of books by providing warm spaces and tackling social isolation. The Public Libraries and Museums Act 1964 places a statutory duty on councils in England and Wales to provide a comprehensive and efficient library service. However, discussions with people in the sector suggest that a lack of clarity around what this actually means creates ambiguity and can lead to library provision being treated as discretionary rather than a legal duty. I think you have gone some way to answering the question in terms of that long-term strategy, but would the Government consider looking to give more clarity on what constitutes a comprehensive and efficient library service and provide councils with greater certainty about their statutory responsibilities?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae llyfrgelloedd yn wasanaethau hanfodol i bobl o bob oed, ac yn aml yn mynd ymhell y tu hwnt i roi benthyg llyfrau drwy ddarparu mannau cynnes a mynd i'r afael ag ynysigrwydd cymdeithasol. Mae Deddf Llyfrgelloedd Cyhoeddus ac Amgueddfeydd 1964 yn gosod dyletswydd statudol ar gynghorau yng Nghymru a Lloegr i ddarparu gwasanaeth llyfrgell cynhwysfawr ac effeithlon. Fodd bynnag, mae trafodaethau gyda phobl yn y sector yn awgrymu bod diffyg eglurder ynghylch beth y mae hyn yn ei olygu mewn gwirionedd yn creu amwysedd ac y gall hynny arwain at drin darpariaeth llyfrgell fel rhywbeth disgresiynol yn hytrach na dyletswydd gyfreithiol. Rwy'n credu eich bod wedi ateb rhywfaint o'r cwestiwn ynglŷn â'r strategaeth hirdymor honno, ond a wnaiff y Llywodraeth ystyried rhoi mwy o eglurder ynghylch beth sy'n cyfrif fel gwasanaeth llyfrgell cynhwysfawr ac effeithlon a rhoi mwy o sicrwydd i gynghorau ynghylch eu cyfrifoldebau statudol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn pellach hwnnw. Yng Nghymru, mae gennym ni fframwaith safonau llyfrgelloedd cyhoeddus Cymru, sef y mesur a ddefnyddir i benderfynu a yw hyn yn cael ei fodloni ai peidio. Mae hwn yn fater byw iawn. Dwi'n ymwybodol o'r pryderon sydd ledled Cymru, ac un o'r pethau dwi'n edrych arnyn nhw ydy beth ydy'r cyfrifoldebau a'r grym sydd gen i o dan y Ddeddf honno os nad ydy'r gwasanaethau hynny yn cyrraedd y safon ddisgwyliedig. Wrth i'r gwaith o ddatblygu'r strategaeth newydd fynd rhagddo, byddwn ni hefyd yn cyhoeddi cynlluniau penodol sy'n edrych ar bob sector, gan gynnwys llyfrgelloedd, er mwyn rhoi rhagor o eglurder, ie, i awdurdodau lleol, ond hefyd i bobl Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for that further question. In Wales, we have a public library standards framework, which is the measure that is used to decide whether the quality of libraries has been met or not. This is a very live issue. I am aware of the concerns that exist across Wales, and one of the things that I am looking at is what responsibilities and powers I have under that Act if those services do not reach the mark in terms of quality. As the work of developing the new strategy goes forward, we will also be publishing specific plans looking at every sector, including libraries, in order to provide more clarity, yes, to local authorities, but also to the people of Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Henebion Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: National Monuments

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn diogelu ac yn hyrwyddo henebion cenedlaethol Gwynedd Maldwyn ar gyfer cenedlaethau’r dyfodol? OQ64676
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. How is the Welsh Government protecting and promoting national monuments in Gwynedd Maldwyn for future generations? OQ64676

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae Cadw yn gwarchod ac yn hyrwyddo henebion o bwysigrwydd cenedlaethol yng Ngwynedd Maldwyn drwy eu dynodi a thrwy ddarparu cyngor arbenigol, arweiniad a chymorth i'w perchnogion ar gyfer eu cadwraeth. Mae Cadw hefyd yn hyrwyddo ein treftadaeth drwy reoli'r henebion cenedlaethol sydd yn ei ofal a sicrhau mynediad cyhoeddus atyn nhw, yn unol ag ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth hon i hyrwyddo mynediad teg i'n safleoedd diwylliannol a threftadaeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Cadw protects and promotes nationally important monuments in Gwynedd Maldwyn through designation and through providing expert advice, guidance and support to the owners for their conservation. Cadw also promotes our heritage by managing the national monuments in its care and ensuring public access to them, in accordance with this Government's commitment to provide fair access to all of our cultural and heritage sites.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Fe fyddwch yn ymwybodol fod Llansilin yn etholaeth Gwynedd Maldwyn yn gartref i Sycharth, llys hynafol Owain Glyndŵr ac un o safleoedd mwyaf arwyddocaol ein treftadaeth genedlaethol. Yn anffodus, fodd bynnag, mae'n gywilyddus nad yw cyflwr presennol y safle yn adlewyrchu ei bwysigrwydd hanesyddol a chenedlaethol. Ceir problemau megis gordyfiant, diffyg mynediad hygyrch, a hyd yn oed diffyg crybwyll i'r safle ar wefan Cadw. Ar y llaw arall, mae Cyngor Sir Powys eisoes wedi gwrthod ymdrechion am fwy o arwyddion pwrpasol ar y ffyrdd i hyrwyddo'r lle. A gaf i ofyn, felly, sut y gall Llywodraeth Cymru gydweithio â Cadw a Chyngor Sir Powys i sicrhau bod Sycharth yn cael ei hyrwyddo fel safle o bwysigrwydd genedlaethol ar gyfer cenedlaethau'r dyfodol?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: You will be aware that Llansilin in the Gwynedd Maldwyn constituency is the home of Sycharth, the ancient court of Owain Glyndŵr and one of the most significant sites of our national heritage. Unfortunately, however, it is disgraceful that the current state of the site doesn't reflect its historic and national importance. There are problems such as overgrowing foliage, lack of access and even a lack of mention of the site on the Cadw website. On the other hand, Powys council has already rejected proposals for more signage on the road to promote the site. Can I ask, therefore, how the Welsh Government can work with Cadw and Powys County Council to ensure that Sycharth is promoted as a site of national importance for future generations?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi Sycharth. I fi fod yn glir, dwi yn ystyried bod Sycharth yn heneb o bwys cenedlaethol sydd â lle arwyddocaol yn hanes Cymru ac yn ein hunaniaeth ni fel cenedl. Mae'r heneb ar agor i'r cyhoedd. Mae yna arwyddion dehongli ar y safle. Yn sgil rhaglen o waith cadwraeth a gynhaliwyd gyda chyllid gan Cadw, mae yna waith wedi mynd rhagddo ers i bryderon gael eu codi rai blynyddoedd yn ôl. Ond, mi ydw i ar y record yn dweud y byddwn i'n hoffi gweld mwy yn cael ei wneud i hyrwyddo Sycharth cyn i fi fod yn y rôl hon, a dwi'n dal o'r farn honno. Er bod lleoliad gwledig a natur y safle yn peri rhai heriau o ran mynediad ffisegol a'r ffordd y mae'n cael ei gyflwyno, mi ydw i wedi gofyn i Cadw ymchwilio i sut y gellir gwneud stori'r safle hwn yn fwy amlwg gan ei fod o mor, mor bwysig o ran ein hanes ni. Fe fyddwch chi hefyd yn ymwybodol nad yw Sycharth ar werth ar hyn o bryd. Mae o'n destun tenantiaeth gydol oes. Mae Cadw yn gweithio mewn partneriaeth efo'r ystâd sy'n berchen ar Sycharth i sicrhau ei fod yn cael ei gynnal a'i gadw mewn cyflwr da a bod mynediad i'r cyhoedd yn parhau.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising the issue of Sycharth. Just to be clear, I do consider Sycharth to be a monument of national importance that has a very significant place in Wales's history and in our identity as a nation. The monument is open to the public. There are interpretation signs on the site. After a conservation programme carried out with funding by Cadw, work has gone ahead since concerns were raised a few years ago. However, I am on the record as saying that I would like to see more being done to promote Sycharth before I was in this role, and I'm still of that opinion. Even though the rural location and nature of the site do present some problems in terms of physical access and the way it's presented, I have asked Cadw to look into how we can make the story of this site more prominent, because it is just so important in terms of our history. You will also be aware that Sycharth isn't for sale at the moment. It has a lifetime tenancy. Cadw is working in partnership with the estate that owns Sycharth to ensure that it is maintained and kept in good condition and that public access continues.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Following on from that question about protecting our historic heritage for future generations, last week, I had a meeting with Historic Houses Wales. A great deal of our heritage is actually in private ownership. I know from personal experience of living in a grade II listed house just how expensive these properties can be to maintain, particularly when there are restrictions on making improvements to reduce running costs. Can I ask the Cabinet Minister what practical support is available through Cadw for private owners who are helping to preserve our historic heritage, and how is she working with colleagues across Government to make sure these buildings remain viable for future generations?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn dilyn y cwestiwn hwnnw ynglŷn â diogelu ein treftadaeth hanesyddol ar gyfer cenedlaethau'r dyfodol, yr wythnos diwethaf, cefais gyfarfod â Tai Hanesyddol Cymru. Mae llawer iawn o'n treftadaeth mewn perchnogaeth breifat mewn gwirionedd. Gwn o brofiad personol o fyw mewn tŷ rhestredig gradd II pa mor ddrud y gall eiddo o'r fath fod i'w gynnal, yn enwedig pan fo cyfyngiadau ar wneud gwelliannau i leihau costau rhedeg. A gaf i ofyn i'r Gweinidog Cabinet pa gymorth ymarferol sydd ar gael drwy Cadw i berchnogion preifat sy'n helpu i ddiogelu ein treftadaeth hanesyddol, a sut y mae'n gweithio gyda chyd-Aelodau ar draws y Llywodraeth i sicrhau bod yr adeiladau hyn yn parhau'n hyfyw ar gyfer cenedlaethau'r dyfodol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn pellach hwnnw. Mi wnes i a swyddogion o Cadw gyfarfod efo Historic Houses Wales yr wythnos diwethaf, ac mi fydd swyddogion yn trafod ymhellach efo nhw o ran sut mae mynd rhagddo efo unrhyw waith cefnogaeth ac i archwilio beth yw'r opsiynau posib. Yn amlwg, mae yna gyfle iddyn nhw hefyd gyfrannu fel rhan o ddatblygiad y strategaeth newydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for that further question. I and Cadw officials did meet with Historic Houses Wales last week, and officials will be having further discussions with them in relation to how we can proceed with any support work and to look at any possible options. Clearly, there is an opportunity also for them to contribute as part of the development of our new strategy.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Lefarwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from Party Spokespeople

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf nawr ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Llefarydd Reform UK, Louise Emery.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. The Reform UK spokesperson, Louise Emery.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Minister, I had a question to the First Minister on 29 September about business rates and music venues—and I welcome the 30 per cent reduction—that talked about the cliff edge that happens at the £51,000 business rate edge. I want to keep this issue front and centre of your mind when you're in discussions with the finance Minister. A lot of cultural activities require public money to exist, and we don't want music venues to join that list. They want to be self-sufficient, they don't want to rely on grants, and this is a way we can help them. So, can I ask will you address the exclusion of music venues with the finance Minister, including consideration of a business rates taper approach in the future? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Weinidog, roedd gennyf gwestiwn i'r Prif Weinidog ar 29 Medi ynglŷn ag ardrethi busnes a lleoliadau cerddoriaeth—ac rwy'n croesawu'r gostyngiad o 30 y cant—a oedd yn ymwneud â'r ymyl clogwyn ar £51,000 mewn perthynas ag ardrethi busnes. Rwyf am ichi roi ystyriaeth i'r mater hwn pan fyddwch chi'n trafod gyda'r Gweinidog cyllid. Mae angen arian cyhoeddus ar lawer o weithgareddau diwylliannol i fodoli, ac nid ydym am i leoliadau cerddoriaeth ymuno â'r rhestr honno. Maent eisiau bod yn hunangynhaliol, nid ydynt eisiau dibynnu ar grantiau, ac mae hon yn un ffordd y gallwn eu helpu. Felly, a gaf i ofyn ichi drafod eithrio lleoliadau cerddoriaeth gyda'r Gweinidog cyllid, gan gynnwys ystyried dull tapro ar gyfer ardrethi busnes yn y dyfodol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Fe fyddwch chi yn gwerthfawrogi mai cwestiynau i fi ydy'r rhain, ac mae'n bosib holi'r Gweinidog cyllid yn y set nesaf o gwestiynau o ran hynny. Ond, yn sicr, o ran dyfodol lleoliadau cerddoriaeth, mae o'n rheswm pam mae'r 30 y cant yna wedi'i gyhoeddi, i gefnogi lleoliadau llai. Mi fyddwn ni hefyd yn edrych ar hyn fel rhan o'r strategaeth diwylliant newydd. O ran dyfodol cerddoriaeth yng Nghymru yn ei chyfanrwydd, mae peth cyfrifoldeb am gerddoriaeth rŵan efo Cymru Greadigol ac mae peth cyfrifoldeb am gerddoriaeth yn dod o dan Gyngor Celfyddydau Cymru. Mae yna amwysedd weithiau o ran pwy sy'n gyfrifol am y sector hwn yng Nghymru, oherwydd, yn amlwg, mae'n bwysig o ran economi Cymru hefyd, ac i ganol ein trefi ni a chymaint o gymunedau ledled Cymru. Yr hyn rydyn ni'n benderfynol, fel Llywodraeth, o wneud yw gweithio yn draws-weinidogol, trawsbortffolio i sicrhau bod y strategaeth newydd yn cymryd i ystyriaeth fudd cerddoriaeth, ie, o ran iechyd a lles, o ran diwylliant Cymru, ond hefyd o ran yr economi. Felly, mae hwn yn fater byw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. You will appreciate that these are questions to me, and you may want to ask that question of the finance Minister in the next set of questions. But, certainly, in terms of the future of music venues, it is one of the reasons why that 30 per cent was announced, in order to support smaller venues. We will also be looking at this as part of the new culture strategy. In terms of the future of music in Wales in its entirety, some responsibility for music lies with Creative Wales, and some of the responsibility for music falls to the Wales Arts Council. There is some ambiguity on occasion as to who is responsible for this sector in Wales, because, clearly, it's important for the Welsh economy too, along with our town centres and so many communities the length and breadth of Wales. What we as a Government to determine to do is to work on a cross-ministerial and cross-portfolio basis in order to ensure that the new strategy does take into account the benefit of music, yes, in terms of health and well-being, the culture of Wales, but also in terms of our economy. So, this is a very live issue.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Now, I'd like an update on the national museum in Cardiff. Now, we know that we got some funding for roof repairs earlier this year, and you came to our culture committee and expressed concern about water entering galleries containing our national collections. We've got winter approaching, and it's important that we have essential maintenance that carries on. But I want to know what progress there's been on the funding and repairs and what timetable and funding are in place to complete the urgent works, because we could be in a position where not only that our collections are at risk, but that the museum actually has to close.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Nawr, hoffwn yr wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am yr amgueddfa genedlaethol yng Nghaerdydd. Nawr, fe wyddom inni gael rhywfaint o arian ar gyfer atgyweirio'r to yn gynharach eleni, a daethoch at ein pwyllgor diwylliant a mynegi pryder am ddŵr yn mynd i mewn i orielau sy'n cynnwys ein casgliadau cenedlaethol. Mae'r gaeaf yn agosáu, ac mae'n hollbwysig fod y gwaith cynnal a chadw hanfodol yn parhau. Ond hoffwn wybod pa gynnydd a wnaed ar y cyllid a'r atgyweiriadau a pha amserlen a pha gyllid sydd ar waith i gwblhau'r gwaith brys, gan y gallem fod mewn sefyllfa lle nid yn unig y byddai ein casgliadau mewn perygl, ond byddai'n rhaid i’r amgueddfa gau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn hwn. Fel roeddwn i'n dweud wrth fod gerbron y pwyllgor ac fel rydych chi wedi sôn, dwi'n bryderus dros ben ynglŷn ag Amgueddfa Genedlaethol Caerdydd a dwi'n edrych ymlaen i dderbyn cynigion ar gyfer yr ailddatblygu posib gan Amgueddfa Genedlaethol Caerdydd. Dwi heb gael y manylion hynny hyd yma. Yr hyn rydyn ni wedi bod yn ei wneud ydy gweithio'n agos iawn gydag Amgueddfa Cymru i geisio deall beth ydy'r sefyllfa a beth ydy'r angen, ac mi ydyn ni wedi dyrannu hyd at £4.8 miliwn mewn arian cyfalaf yn y flwyddyn ariannol yma i gefnogi'r gwaith gwella mwyaf brys ac i helpu i ddiogelu'r casgliadau. Mae'r rhain yn gwestiynau dwi hefyd wedi bod yn eu holi i Amgueddfa Cymru, a dwi'n edrych ymlaen at gael diweddariad arnyn nhw ac i fedru rhannu'r wybodaeth yna'n fwy eang pan fydd y wybodaeth gen i.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for that question. As I said when I appeared before the committee, and as you have mentioned, I am extremely concerned about National Museum Cardiff, and I am looking forward to receiving proposals for the possible redevelopment from the national museum. I haven't received the details to date. What we have been doing is working very closely with Amgueddfa Cymru to try and understand what the position is and what the needs are, and we have allocated up to £4.8 million in capital funding in this financial year to support the most urgent remedial work and to help to secure the collections. These are questions that I too have been asking of Amgueddfa Cymru, and I look forward to receiving an update on them and to sharing that information more broadly when I have it.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Okay. Finally, I want to talk about the Tour de France. It's coming to Wales next summer, starting in Welshpool and finishing in Cardiff. We want it to be a successful event to showcase Wales, to help the local economy and be a great event for all of us to attend. But events of this scale cost money to host. We totally accept that; that's the deal. But we want transparency around these costs now and in the build-up to the event, and in the legacy funding afterwards. Now, I know you've announced the £4.5 million legacy fund, and I've got a query about that and then a question about the hosting fees. The legacy fund comes from the brilliant basics fund, or is administered through the brilliant basics fund, which is to provide small tourism infrastructure projects. Is this additional money, the £4.5 million, noting that it's going to be ring-fenced for cycling infrastructure, or is it just part of the brilliant basics fund, so it's going to come out of that original pot? That's my first question. And secondly, on the hosting fee, which public body has paid for this? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Iawn. Yn olaf, hoffwn sôn am y Tour de France. Bydd yn dod i Gymru yn yr haf, gan ddechrau yn y Trallwng a gorffen yng Nghaerdydd. Rydym am iddo fod yn ddigwyddiad llwyddiannus i arddangos Cymru, i helpu’r economi leol a bod yn ddigwyddiad gwych i bob un ohonom ei fynychu. Ond mae digwyddiadau ar y raddfa hon yn costio arian i'w cynnal. Rydym yn derbyn hynny’n llwyr; dyna’r fargen. Ond rydym eisiau tryloywder ynghylch y costau hyn nawr, ac yn y cyfnod cyn y digwyddiad, ac yn y cyllid gwaddol wedi hynny. Nawr, gwn eich bod wedi cyhoeddi'r gronfa waddol £4.5 miliwn, ac mae gennyf gwestiwn am hynny ac yna cwestiwn am y ffioedd cynnal. Daw’r gronfa waddol o’r gronfa pethau pwysig, neu fe gaiff ei gweinyddu drwy’r gronfa pethau pwysig, sydd ar gyfer darparu prosiectau seilwaith twristiaeth bach. A yw'r arian ychwanegol hwn, y £4.5 miliwn, yn nodi ei fod yn mynd i gael ei glustnodi ar gyfer seilwaith beicio, neu a yw'n rhan o'r gronfa pethau pwysig, felly bydd yn dod o'r pot gwreiddiol hwnnw? Dyna fy nghwestiwn cyntaf. Ac yn ail, o ran y ffi cynnal, pa gorff cyhoeddus sydd wedi talu am hyn? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n hapus i ddarparu gwybodaeth ychwanegol. Mae rhan gyntaf eich cwestiwn chi at Weinidog arall, sef Adam Price; nid yw'n rhan o fy mhortffolio i. Mae yna gydweithio agos ar y funud yn draws-weinidogol o ran y Tour de France. Fyddwch chi hefyd yn gwerthfawrogi ein bod ni wedi etifeddu'r Tour de France, ac un o'r pethau dwi ar y record yn dweud ydy bod rhain yn bethau y dylai unrhyw lywodraeth edrych arnyn nhw cyn mynd am unrhyw ddigwyddiad mawr. Mi ddylai'r holl wybodaeth yma fod yn wybyddus cyn i ni hyd yn oed roi'r cais i mewn. Dydy'r eglurder yna ddim yna. Felly, ar y funud, yr hyn dŷn ni'n ei wneud ydy gweithio'n draws-weinidogol i ddeall yn well ba symiau gwahanol sydd mewn gwahanol bortffolios ar y funud, a hefyd, o ran edrych ar y gwaddol, sut ydyn ni'n cydlynu'r holl waith hwnnw i sicrhau bod yr impact mwyaf a'r gwaddol mwyaf yn dod o hyn. Ond, i fi fod yn glir, wrth i ni fel Llywodraeth fynd rhagddi, dyma'r math o newid fydd, sef edrych ar gynllunio manwl cyn i ni roi cais i mewn, ac nid, fel rydym ni wedi gweld o dan Lafur, yn meddwl wedyn ar ôl i rywbeth ddod i Gymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I'm happy to provide additional information. The first part of your question should be referred to another minister, Adam Price, as it's not part of my portfolio. There is close collaboration on a cross-ministerial basis on the Tour de France. You will also appreciate that we inherited the Tour de France, and one of the things that I'm on the record as having said is that these are things that any government should look at before bidding for any major event. All of that information should be known before we even make that application. That clarity isn't there. So, at the moment, what we are doing is working on a cross-ministerial basis to better understand what different pots of money are in different portfolios currently, and also, in terms of looking at the legacy, how we can co-ordinate all of that work in order to ensure the greatest possible impact and the greatest possible legacy from all of this. But, for me to be clear, as we as a Government proceed, this is the kind of change that you will see—we will be looking at detailed planning before making applications, and not, as we saw under Labour, doing the thinking once something has been delivered for Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Mike Hedges.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Labour spokesperson, Mike Hedges.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. I want to raise a question on esports, which, as most people I think know, is short for electronic sports, which refers to organised competitive video gaming where individuals or teams compete in specific games for prizes, ranking or prestige. Esports have developed from a casual hobby into a structured global industry with leagues, governing bodies, teams, sponsors and dedicated venues. In Wales, the industry is growing rapidly. From my days of being a college lecturer, it was very popular. Esports Wales runs multiple official tournaments throughout the Welsh esports league, and the student esports championships. These events include seasonal leagues, open tournaments and school and college competitions, with structured formats and prize money. Will the Minister dedicate some of the money given to support the creative industries to esports as part of a comprehensive esports strategy?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Rwyf am godi cwestiwn ynglŷn ag e-chwaraeon, sydd, fel y gŵyr y rhan fwyaf o bobl, rwy’n credu, yn golygu chwaraeon electronig, sy’n cyfeirio at ornestau gemau fideo cystadleuol wedi’u trefnu lle mae unigolion neu dimau’n cystadlu mewn gemau penodol am wobrau, safle neu fri. Mae e-chwaraeon wedi datblygu o hobi achlysurol i fod yn ddiwydiant byd-eang strwythuredig gyda chynghreiriau, cyrff llywodraethu, timau, noddwyr a lleoliadau pwrpasol. Yng Nghymru, mae’r diwydiant yn tyfu’n gyflym. O fy nyddiau fel darlithydd coleg, roedd yn boblogaidd iawn. Mae Esports Cymru yn cynnal nifer o dwrnameintiau swyddogol drwy gynghrair e-chwaraeon Cymru, a'r bencampwriaeth e-chwaraeon i fyfyrwyr. Mae'r digwyddiadau hyn yn cynnwys cynghreiriau tymhorol, pencampwriaethau agored a chystadlaethau ysgolion a cholegau gyda fformatau strwythuredig a gwobrau ariannol. A wnaiff y Gweinidog glustnodi rhywfaint o'r arian a roddir i gefnogi'r diwydiannau creadigol i e-chwaraeon fel rhan o strategaeth chwaraeon gynhwysfawr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am fod yn rhywun sydd yn codi esports, a dwi'n cytuno efo chi—mae angen gwneud mwy o ran e-chwaraeon. Does dim digon o strategaeth wedi bod na digon o werthfawrogiad o'i bwysigrwydd o yma yng Nghymru. Drwy Cymru Greadigol, rydyn ni wedi cefnogi nifer o brosiectau ar y cyd ag E-chwaraeon Cymru. Mae'r prosiectau hyn wedi datblygu sgiliau digidol, technegol a darlledu, wedi codi ymwybyddiaeth o yrfaoedd creadigol a chryfhau llwybrau i gemau sgrin a chyfryngau digidol. Mi fydda i yn cwrdd ag Esports Wales cyn bo hir, a dwi'n edrych ymlaen at fynd â'r sgwrs yna'n bellach. Yn amlwg, wrth i'r gwaith fynd rhagddo, rwy'n hapus iawn i ddiweddaru'r Aelod, a hefyd holl Aelodau'r Senedd, ar y gwaith hwnnw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for being someone that does raise esports frequently, and I agree with you—we do need to do more in terms of esports. There hasn't been enough of a strategy or enough appreciation of their importance here in Wales. Through Creative Wales, we have supported a number of joint projects with Esports Wales. A number of these projects have developed digital skills, technical skills, broadcasting skills, and have raised awareness and strengthened pathways to the future. I will meet shortly with Esports Wales, and I look forward to carrying on that discussion. Clearly, as the work goes ahead, I am very content to update the Member, and also all Members of the Senedd, on this work.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you very much for that answer. As you may remember, in November 2024, the then Minister for Culture, Skills and Social Partnership, Jack Sargeant, took part in a landmark event in the Senedd to promote Wales's thriving esports industry and the Government's commitment to providing the safest and most engaging environment for young gamers. At the event, the Minister said that esports

'is a priority sector for the Welsh Government and I’m keen do all I can to support its growth and gain an international reputation for Wales as a centre for this rapidly growing industry.'

Esports Wales have garnered significant success in recent years, with notable achievements, such as winning a gold medal in the Rocket League open competition at the Commonwealth Esports Championships. The team also secured a silver medal in the eFootball women's competition and a bronze in the eFootball open competition. I was very pleased, in the event we had here, to see Peter Fox in action playing esports. Are esports a priority for this Government, and have they a date for another esports event at the Senedd?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn am eich ateb. Fel y cofiwch, efallai, ym mis Tachwedd 2024, cymerodd y Gweinidog Diwylliant, Sgiliau a Phartneriaeth Gymdeithasol ar y pryd, Jack Sargeant, ran mewn digwyddiad nodedig yn y Senedd i hyrwyddo diwydiant e-chwaraeon ffyniannus Cymru ac ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth i ddarparu'r amgylchedd mwyaf diogel a mwyaf deniadol i chwaraewyr ifanc. Yn y digwyddiad, dywedodd y Gweinidog fod e-chwaraeon

'yn sector â blaenoriaeth i Lywodraeth Cymru ac rwy'n awyddus i wneud popeth yn fy ngallu i gefnogi ei dwf a sicrhau enw da rhyngwladol i Gymru fel canolfan ar gyfer y diwydiant hwn sy'n tyfu'n gyflym.'

Mae Esports Cymru wedi cael llwyddiant sylweddol yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf, gyda chyflawniadau nodedig, fel ennill medal aur yn y gystadleuaeth agored Rocket League ym Mhencampwriaeth E-chwaraeon y Gymanwlad. Sicrhaodd y tîm fedal arian hefyd yn y gystadleuaeth eFootball i fenywod a medal efydd yn y gystadleuaeth eFootball agored. Roeddwn yn falch iawn, yn y digwyddiad a gawsom yma, o weld Peter Fox yn chwarae e-chwaraeon. A yw e-chwaraeon yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon, ac a oes ganddynt ddyddiad ar gyfer digwyddiad e-chwaraeon arall yn y Senedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch i'r Aelod. Dwi'n gobeithio fy mod i wedi ateb rhan o'r cwestiwn yna yn fy ymateb cyntaf, sef ydw, dwi'n credu eu bod nhw'n bwysig a dwi'n credu y dylid gwneud mwy. Yn wahanol i Weinidogion yn y gorffennol, dwi ddim yn credu mewn geiriau cynnes yn unig—dwi'n credu mewn gweithredu a chael strategaeth yn ei lle. Felly, mae'r ffaith eich bod chi'n dal i holi'r cwestiwn hwnnw, er i'r ymrwymiad gael ei wneud gan Weinidog Llafur blaenorol yn 2024, yn dweud y cyfan, mae arnaf ofn, o ran y portffolio dwi wedi ei etifeddu.

Yn sicr, mae angen gwneud mwy. Dwi'n rhoi'r ymrwymiad hynny, ac mi fyddaf yn trafod yn bellach efo Esports Wales. Mi wnes i hefyd mynychu'r digwyddiad hwnnw a chymryd rhan mewn rhai o'r esports. Na, doeddwn i ddim yn dda iawn, ond roedd yn dda iawn gweld esports ar waith yma yn y Senedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank the Member. I hope that I have responded to that question in my first response. Yes, I do think that they're important, and I think more needs to be done. And unlike Ministers in the past, I don't just believe in warm words—I believe in taking action and putting a strategy in place. So the fact that you're still asking that question, despite the commitment being made by a previous Labour Minister in 2024, says it all, I'm afraid, in terms of the portfolio I've inherited.

Certainly, we do need to do more. I give you that commitment, and I will discuss further with Esports Wales. I also attended that event, and I took part in some of those esports. No, I wasn't very good at them, but it was very good to see esports in action here in the Senedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Paul Davies.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Conservative spokesperson, Paul Davies.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog, yr wythnos diwethaf, dywedodd aelod o staff Amgueddfa Cymru fod yr amgueddfa genedlaethol wedi dod yn fwyfwy camweithredol yn ystod y blynyddoedd diwethaf. Disgrifiodd ddiwylliant o ddirywiad rheoledig, ystum unigol, a diffyg stiwardiaeth broffesiynol o'r casgliad cenedlaethol. Roedd hefyd wedi codi y gallai unrhyw gyllid cyhoeddus ychwanegol a ddarperir, fel rhan o gynlluniau canmlwyddiant yr amgueddfa, fethu â chyflawni ei amcanion bwriadedig, oni bai bod y materion a nodwyd yn cael eu harchwilio a'u mynd i'r afael â nhw yn iawn. Weinidog, beth yw eich ymateb chi i'r pryderon hyn? Ac yn dilyn ymlaen o'ch atebion cynharach, pa fath o drafodaethau ydych chi wedi eu cael gydag Amgueddfa Cymru i sicrhau hyder y cyhoedd o ran llywodraethu a rheoli ein casgliadau cenedlaethol?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Minister, last week, a member of Amgueddfa Cymru staff said that the national museum had become increasingly dysfunctional and described a culture of managed decline, individual posturing, and a lack of professional stewardship of the national collection. They also raised the fact that any additional public funding provided, as part of the centenary of the museum, could fail to deliver its objectives unless the issues identified were examined and addressed properly. Minister, what is your response to those concerns? And following on from your earlier responses, what kind of discussions have you had with Amgueddfa Cymru to secure public confidence in the governance and management of our national collections?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Mi ydw i'n ymwybodol o'r erthygl a gyhoeddwyd ar y wefan Nation.Cymru yr ydych yn cyfeirio ati. Mi oedd o hefyd yn cynnwys ymateb gan Amgueddfa Cymru. Mi ydw i'n sicr yn fyw iawn i'r cwestiynau sy'n cael eu codi. Dwi eisiau sicrhau, fel pawb ohonoch chi, gwerth am arian. Dwi eisiau sicrhau diogelwch ein casgliadau cenedlaethol a dwi eisiau sicrhau dyfodol ein hamgueddfeydd cenedlaethol ni. Mae yna gwestiynau o ran y sefyllfa dwi wedi'i hetifeddu yr ydw i'n mynd ar eu holau. Mae yna gwestiynau byw iawn o ran sicrhau ein bod ni'n deall sut mae Amgueddfa Genedlaethol Caerdydd wedi cyrraedd sefyllfa lle mae angen cymaint o wariant hefyd.

Dwi eisiau dysgu gwersi fel ein bod ni'n gallu osgoi'r rheini wrth fynd rhagddo, ond yr ymrwymiad dwi'n ei roi i chi ydy ein bod ni'n gweithio gydag Amgueddfa Cymru ar ddatblygu cynigion i'r dyfodol. Ac yn ganolog i bopeth, fel roeddwn i'n ei ddweud, ydy sicrhau dyfodol ein hamgueddfeydd cenedlaethol ni a sicrhau diogelwch ein casgliadau cenedlaethol ni, oherwydd pobl Cymru sydd berchen arnyn nhw—nid y Llywodraeth, nid Amgueddfa Cymru, ond pobl Cymru, ac mae Amgueddfa Cymru yn atebol i bobl Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank the Member for raising this issue. I am aware of that article that was published on Nation.Cymru. It also included a response from Amgueddfa Cymru. I certainly am very alive to the questions that are being raised. I, like all of you, want to ensure value for money. I want to ensure the safety of our national collections, and I want to ensure a future for our national museums. There are questions in terms of the situation that I have inherited, and I am pursuing those. There are very live issues in terms of ensuring that we understand how National Museum Cardiff has reached this position where so much expenditure is needed.

I want to learn lessons so that we can avoid making the same mistakes going forward. But the commitment I give you is that we are working with Amgueddfa Cymru on developing proposals for the future. And central to everything that we want to do, as I said, is ensuring the future of our national museums and safeguarding our national collections, because they belong to the people of Wales—not the Government, not the museum, but the people of Wales, and Amgueddfa Cymru is answerable to the people of Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae sector diwylliant a chelfyddydau Cymru mewn cyfnod hollbwysig, ac mae’r dyfodol ar hyn o bryd yn edrych yn fregus iawn. Yn y cyfamser, mae amgueddfeydd cenedlaethol ledled y byd yn trawsnewid yn ofodau mwy rhyngweithiol, sy’n cael eu gyrru gan dechnoleg i ymgysylltu â chynulleidfaoedd newydd. Er enghraifft, mae’r Smithsonian wedi defnyddio podlediadau yn llwyddiannus i ddod â hanes a diwylliant i gynulleidfaoedd y tu hwnt i’w safleoedd ffisegol nhw. Mae’r Louvre wedi partneru â Snapchat i ddefnyddio offer dehongli arloesol ar gyfer chwech o’i hadrannau. Ac mae amgueddfa dwyrain V&A wedi cynnal rhaglen hwyrnos, sy’n dod â phreswylfeydd DJ, bariau dros dro, a mynediad i arddangosfeydd ar ôl oriau ynghyd.

Felly, Weinidog, pa gefnogaeth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei darparu i helpu amgueddfeydd a sefydliadau diwylliannol yng Nghymru i foderneiddio, fel eu bod yn berthnasol, yn hygyrch ac yn gystadleuol mewn oes sy’n gynyddol ddigidol ac sy’n cael ei arwain gan brofiad? A beth arall y gall Llywodraeth Cymru ei wneud i helpu amgueddfeydd i ddenu cynulleidfaoedd newydd, a denu cynulleidfaoedd iau hefyd?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
The culture and arts sector in Wales is at a crucial point, and the future now looks very vulnerable indeed. In the meantime, national museums across the globe are transforming into more interactive spaces, which are driven by technology, to engage with new audiences. For example, the Smithsonian has used podcasting successfully to bring history and culture to audiences beyond their physical sites. The Louvre has partnered with Snapchat to develop innovative interpretation equipment for six of its sections. And the V&A East museum has held a late-night programme, bringing together DJ residencies, temporary bars and access to exhibitions after hours. 

So, Minister, what support is the Welsh Government providing to assist museums and other cultural organisations in Wales to modernise, so that they are relevant, accessible and competitive in an age that is increasingly digital and experience led? And what else can the Welsh Government do to help museums to attract new audiences, and to attract younger audiences too?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dwi’n meddwl y byddwch chi yn debygol iawn rŵan o dderbyn gwahoddiad gan Amgueddfa Cymru i fynychu rhai o’u digwyddiadau hwyrnos nhw. Dwi heb fynychu fy hun, ond mae nhw eisoes wedi bod yn gwneud hyn, ac mae wedi bod yn wych gweld y croesdoriad o oedrannau wrth i’r gofodau hyn ddod yn fyw ar adeg o’r nos pan dwi fel arfer yn fy ngwely erbyn hyn, yn anffodus. Ond mae yna waith arloesol yn digwydd.

Dwi wedi gweld esiamplau gwych o hyn ledled Cymru. Mae yna esiamplau wedi bod o allu aros dros nos yn rhai o’n hamgueddfeydd ni ac ati, efo’ch plant, night at the museum—ddim cweit fel y ffilm, ond y math yna o awyrgylch. Felly, dwi ddim eisiau rhoi'r argraff nad ydyn ni'n arloesi yma yng Nghymru. Ydw i’n credu bod yna fwy o gyfleoedd? Ydw. Ydw i’n credu, drwy’r strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon, ei bod hi’n angenrheidiol bod digidol yn fwy amlwg? Ydw, yn sicr.

Felly, dwi’n meddwl bod angen adeiladu ar y gwaith arloesol sy’n digwydd, ac edrych ar y math o bethau y gallem ni fod yn eu gwneud yma yng Nghymru. Trwy ddod â’r diwydiannau creadigol yn rhan o’r strategaeth ddiwylliant, dwi’n meddwl bod yna gyfle hefyd i ddatblygu partneriaethau rhwng y diwydiannau creadigol a’n sefydliadau diwylliannol ni, a bod hwnna’n rhan o’r strategaeth o ran yr economi hefyd. Felly, mae yna gyfleoedd i wneud mwy, ond mae yna arloesi eisoes yn digwydd. Mae eisiau gweld mwy ohono fo, a mwy o fuddsoddi yn y strategaeth y tu ôl i hynny.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I think you are very likely to receive an invitation shortly from Amgueddfa Cymru to go to some their late-night events. I haven't attended any of those myself, but they have been doing these for quite a while now, and it's been great to see that cross-section of ages as these spaces become live at a time of night when I'm usually in bed, unfortunately. But there is very innovative work going on. 

I have seen excellent examples of this across Wales. There have been examples of being able to stay overnight in some of our museums and so on, with your children, a night at the museum—not quite like the film, but that kind of atmosphere. So, I don't want to give the impression that we are not innovating here in Wales. Do I believe that there are more opportunities we could pursue? Yes. Do I believe that through our new culture and sport strategy it is necessary that digital is more prominent? Yes, I certainly do.

So, I think that we need to build on the innovative work that's happening, looking at the kind of things that we could be doing here in Wales. And by bringing the creative industries into that culture strategy, I think there is also an opportunity to develop partnerships between the creative industries and our cultural institutions, and that that is part of the strategy for the economy as well. So, there are opportunities to do more, but there is already innovation going on. We need to see more of that, and more investment in the strategy underlying it.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa gamau mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn eu cymryd i sicrhau nad yw'r gost a'r lleoliad yn atal pobl ifanc rhag cymryd rhan mewn chwaraeon? OQ64703
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What action is the Cabinet Minister taking to ensure that cost and location do not prevent young people from participating in sport? OQ64703

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae hyn yn ganolog i’n gweledigaeth ni ar gyfer y strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon newydd. Yn ein 100 diwrnod cyntaf mewn Llywodraeth, fe wnaethom ni gomisiynu archwiliad i gyfleusterau chwaraeon ledled Cymru, a thrwy Chwaraeon Cymru, mi rydyn ni’n buddsoddi mewn cyfleoedd lleol sydd yn fforddiadwy, yn cefnogi clybiau cymunedol i wella cyfleusterau, gyda gweithredu wedi’i dargedu i gyrraedd y rhai sy’n wynebu’r rhwystrau mwyaf o ran cyfranogiad.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: This is central to our vision for the culture and sport strategy. In our first 100 days in Government, we commissioned an investigation into sports facilities across Wales, and through Sport Wales, we are investing in affordable local opportunities, supporting community clubs to improve facilities, with targeted action to reach those who face the greatest barriers to participation.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Drefnydd. In Blaenau Gwent, 49 per cent of children experience income deprivation—that's the highest proportion of any local authority in Wales. Meanwhile, in Caerphilly borough, Cefn Fforest leisure centre has had its hours reduced, with local reports highlighting a massive decline in visits compared to before the change. Behind every lost visit, as we know, is a child disengaging from sport, a missed opportunity and potential left unfulfilled.

Families in deprived communities can't always travel to the next leisure centre, particularly in areas with limited cross-valley transport links. We know that sport improves physical and mental well-being, builds confidence and opens doors for young people. So, what specific investment can Blaenau Gwent, Rhymney and Caerphilly expect, and will you prioritise maintaining vital existing facilities in the deprived communities, rather than directing further investment towards areas that are already better served? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Drefnydd. Ym Mlaenau Gwent, mae 49 y cant o blant yn dioddef yn sgil amddifadedd incwm—y gyfran uchaf o unrhyw awdurdod lleol yng Nghymru. Yn y cyfamser, ym mwrdeistref Caerffili, mae oriau canolfan hamdden Cefn Fforest wedi'u lleihau, gydag adroddiadau lleol yn nodi gostyngiad enfawr mewn ymweliadau o gymharu â chyn y newid. Y tu ôl i bob ymweliad a gollwyd, fel y gwyddom, mae plentyn yn ymddieithrio rhag chwaraeon, cyfle a gollwyd a photensial heb ei gyflawni.

Ni all teuluoedd mewn cymunedau difreintiedig deithio i'r ganolfan hamdden nesaf bob amser, yn enwedig mewn ardaloedd â chysylltiadau trafnidiaeth cyfyngedig rhwng cymoedd. Gwyddom fod chwaraeon yn gwella lles corfforol a meddyliol, yn meithrin hyder ac yn agor drysau i bobl ifanc. Felly, pa fuddsoddiad penodol y gall Blaenau Gwent, Rhymni a Chaerffili ei ddisgwyl, ac a wnewch chi flaenoriaethu cynnal cyfleusterau hanfodol presennol yn y cymunedau difreintiedig, yn hytrach na chyfeirio buddsoddiad pellach tuag at ardaloedd sydd eisoes yn cael eu gwasanaethu'n well? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dwi wedi bod yn glir ers dod yn Weinidog ein bod ni eisiau sicrhau mynediad cydradd i bawb yng Nghymru, a’n bod ni yn cydnabod y rhwystrau sy’n bodoli ar y funud—rhwystrau y mae’n rhaid i fi weithio ar sail trawsbortffolio i'w goresgyn. Dwi’n falch bod Mark Hooper yma rŵan—rydyn ni wedi cael amryw o drafodaethau o ran y rôl mae trafnidiaeth yn ei chwarae o ran galluogi mynediad neu atal mynediad at gyfleusterau a chyfleoedd. Dwi'n gwybod drwy waith achos fy hun am amryw o deuluoedd sydd wedi cysylltu efo fi i ddweud os nad oes ganddyn nhw gar, pa mor heriol ydy o i'w plant nhw fod yn rhan o dîm pêl-droed neu rygbi, oherwydd eu bod nhw'n methu eu cael i gemau ar benwythnosau, gyda llai o glybiau'n gallu fforddio cael bws mini, lle oedd ganddyn nhw yn y gorffennol. Mae'r rhain yn heriau ac nid oes datrysiadau dros nos chwaith.

Mae yna fuddsoddiad yn digwydd drwy'r rhaglen cyfleusterau cymunedol ym Mlaenau Gwent a hefyd drwy Chwaraeon Cymru yng Nghaerffili. Dwi'n meddwl mai'r hyn rydyn ni angen edrych arno fo ydy os ydyn ni'n buddsoddi mewn cyfleusterau, sut wedyn ydyn ni'n cefnogi pobl i oresgyn y rhwystrau eraill sy'n eu hatal nhw rhag cyfranogi. Mae yna raglenni gwych yng Nghaerffili, megis Let's Go Girls, sy'n esiampl wych lle maen nhw'n gallu cefnogi hynny. Ond fel rhan o edrych ar strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon, dwi'n awyddus iawn i glywed yn uniongyrchol gan bobl ifanc a chan deuluoedd am yr heriau y maen nhw'n eu profi rŵan, a byddwn i'n annog pob Aelod o'r Senedd i gyfrannu syniadau at yr hyn a fyddai'n gwneud gwahaniaeth i'ch etholwyr chi.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I have been clear since taking post that we do want to ensure equal access for everyone in Wales, and that we do recognise the barriers that currently exist—barriers that I have to work on a cross-portfolio basis to overcome. I’m pleased that Mark Hooper is here—we’ve had a number of discussions in relation to the role that transport plays in allowing access to opportunities and facilities. I know through my own casework of a number of families who have been in touch with me to say that if they don't have a car, just how challenging it is for their children to be part of a football or rugby team, because they can't get to games on the weekends. Fewer clubs can afford to get minibuses, where they may have done so in the past. These are challenges and there are no overnight solutions.

There is investment taking place through the community facilities programme in Blaenau Gwent and also through Sport Wales in Caerphilly. I do think that what we need to look at is that if we are investing in facilities, how then can we support people to overcome the other barriers preventing them from participating. There are excellent programmes in Caerphilly, such as Let's Go Girls, which is an excellent example where they can provide support. But in looking at the culture and sport strategy more broadly, I'm eager to hear directly from young people and from families about the challenges that they're currently experiencing, and I would encourage all Senedd Members to contribute ideas to what would make a difference to your constituents.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: In Cardiff, affordable indoor sport provision is essential given our reputation as a rainy city, yet rising court and hall hire costs are increasingly pricing out grass-roots clubs and working-class families. At the same time, it took 10 years of campaigning and partnership working between Basketball Wales and Cardiff Council to secure refurbishment of the outdoor courts at Roath Pleasure Gardens—a project that's going to be a genuine game-changer for the local community. Whilst investment in facilities is welcome, many young people still face financial barriers to participation. So, what specific action is the Welsh Government taking to support grass-roots clubs and ensure that a young person's opportunity to play sport is determined by their talent and ambition, not their postcode or their parents' ability to cough up?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yng Nghaerdydd, mae darpariaeth chwaraeon dan do fforddiadwy yn hanfodol o ystyried ein henw fel dinas lawiog, ond fwy a mwy, mae cost gynyddol llogi cyrtiau a neuaddau yn rhy ddrud i glybiau llawr gwlad a theuluoedd dosbarth gweithiol. Ar yr un pryd, cymerodd 10 mlynedd o ymgyrchu a gweithio mewn partneriaeth rhwng Pêl-fasged Cymru a Chyngor Caerdydd i adnewyddu'r cyrtiau awyr agored yng Ngerddi Pleser y Rhath—prosiect a fydd yn gwbl drawsnewidiol i'r gymuned leol. Er bod buddsoddiad mewn cyfleusterau i'w groesawu, mae llawer o bobl ifanc yn dal i wynebu rhwystrau ariannol rhag cymryd rhan. Felly, pa gamau penodol y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gefnogi clybiau llawr gwald a sicrhau bod cyfle unigolyn ifanc i gymryd rhan mewn chwaraeon yn cael ei bennu gan eu talent a'u huchelgais, nid eu cod post na gallu eu rhieni i dalu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Dyna'r union waith rydyn ni yn ei wneud rŵan drwy weithio'n drawsbortffolio. Mae'r ffaith ein bod ni wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau, drwy'r strategaeth tlodi plant newydd, fod diwylliant, chwaraeon a'r cyfranogiad at y rheini'n rhan ganolog o'r gwaith yn bwysig. Dwi'n meddwl bod y ffaith wedi bod yn y gorffennol efallai nad yw hynny wedi bod yn ddigon o ffactor. Rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod am y rhwystrau sydd yna. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod y bwlch o ran cyfranogiad yn cynyddu yn ddibynnol ar incwm teuluol, ac nid dyna sut y dylai hi fod. Felly, dwi'n gofyn i chi, yr holl Aelodau sydd efo esiamplau o brosiectau sy'n gwneud gwahaniaeth, lle ydych chi'n meddwl y dylen ni fod yn canolbwyntio'r adnoddau, i rannu hynny efo ni wrth inni ddatblygu strategaeth sydd wirioneddol yn mynd i fynd i'r afael efo'r heriau hyn. 

Dwi'n cytuno bod yna bocedi gwych o waith yn digwydd yng Nghaerdydd ac mewn gwahanol lefydd o Gymru, ond, yn aml, mae rhai cynlluniau peilota yn dod i ben, er ein bod ni'n gwybod eu bod nhw'n gweithio. Dwi eisiau sicrhau, os oes yna beilot, ein bod ni'n edrych ar a oes yna gyllid ar gael i barhau efo'r gwaith hwnnw. Mae yna hefyd rai cynlluniau lle mae yna nawdd yn dod i mewn, lle mae rhai busnesau sydd efo incwm ac yn gallu rhoi mwy o fudd i mewn i'r gymuned, bod hwnnw wedyn yn cael ei dargedu a'i gefnogi er mwyn caniatáu cynlluniau o'r fath. Does gen i ddim o'r holl atebion o ran 'sut' ar y funud, ond mae hwn yn rhan o'r gwaith rydyn ni'n ei wneud.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you. That's the very work that we're doing now by working on a cross-portfolio basis. The fact that we have committed to ensuring, through the new child poverty strategy, that culture, sport and participation in those is a central part of that work is important. The fact in the past has been that that hasn't been a sufficient factor. We all know of the barriers in place. We all know that the participation gap is widening, reliant on family income, and that's not how it should be. So, I am asking you all, Members who have examples of projects that are truly making a difference, where do you think we should be focusing our resources. Please share those with us as we develop a strategy that truly will tackle these challenges.

I agree that there are excellent pockets of practice in Cardiff and in different parts of Wales, but, often, pilot schemes come to an end, although we know that they work. I do want to ensure, if there is a pilot, that we then look as to whether there is funding available to continue with that work. There are also some projects where sponsorship comes in and some businesses who can provide more into the community, that that is targeted and supported in order to allow those projects to proceed. I don't have all of the solutions in terms of 'how' at the moment, but this is part of the work we're undertaking.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Participating in sport brings many benefits, as we all know. It provides physical health, mental health and well-being, while also providing opportunities to build community and bring people together. But barriers to participation can prevent people from accessing these benefits altogether. Sport Wales's 'State of the Nation' report for 2024-25 notes that two of the three factors most likely to encourage future participation in sport are if there were more facilities, clubs or groups in their area, and if it cost less.

There are pockets in my constituency of Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf, more specifically in Cardiff east, where public transport is infrequent and expensive. And with the decline in youth centres and community facilities in recent years following cuts, it feels as though this problem is only getting worse. I appreciate you've already answered part of this question, but I wanted to ask what action is being taken to measure and address transport-related barriers specifically, and how you're working with the Deputy Minister for Transport to make sure that there is participation for low-income families.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae cymryd rhan mewn chwaraeon yn arwain at lawer o fanteision, fel y gŵyr pob un ohonom. Mae'n gwella iechyd corfforol, iechyd meddwl a lles, ac yn darparu cyfleoedd hefyd i adeiladu cymunedau a dod â phobl ynghyd. Ond gall rhwystrau rhag cymryd rhan atal pobl rhag cael mynediad at y manteision hyn yn gyfan gwbl. Mae adroddiad 'Cyflwr y Genedl' Chwaraeon Cymru ar gyfer 2024-25 yn nodi mai dau o'r tri ffactor sydd fwyaf tebygol o annog cyfranogiad mewn chwaraeon yn y dyfodol yw pe byddai mwy o gyfleusterau, clybiau neu grwpiau yn eu hardal, a phe byddai'n costio llai.

Mae ardaloedd yn fy etholaeth i, Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf, ac yn fwy penodol yn nwyrain Caerdydd, lle mae trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus yn anfynych ac yn ddrud. A chyda'r dirywiad mewn canolfannau ieuenctid a chyfleusterau cymunedol yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf yn dilyn toriadau, mae'n teimlo fel pe bai'r broblem hon ond yn gwaethygu. Rwy'n derbyn eich bod eisoes wedi ateb rhan o'r cwestiwn hwn, ond roeddwn eisiau gofyn pa gamau sy'n cael eu cymryd i fesur a mynd i'r afael â rhwystrau sy'n gysylltiedig â thrafnidiaeth yn benodol, a sut rydych chi'n gweithio gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog Trafnidiaeth i sicrhau bod teuluoedd incwm isel yn gallu cymryd rhan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Fel roeddwn i'n ei ddweud, mae'r rhain yn sgyrsiau byw iawn. Mae'r ffaith bod gyda ni Ddirprwy Brif Weinidog sydd yn arwain ar dlodi plant, bod gyda ni Mark Hooper sydd yn arwain ar drafnidiaeth, bod gyda chi fi, bod gennym ni Nerys Evans, sydd yn edrych o ran yr ochr iechyd ataliol ac iechyd cyhoeddus, yn cydweithio ar hyn er mwyn sicrhau bod y cynlluniau rydyn ni'n eu rhoi yn mynd i'r afael â'r heriau yma, gobeithio yn rhoi'r sicrwydd i chi ein bod ni i gyd yn gweld y rôl sydd gennym ni i'w chwarae. Dwi ddim jest yma'n sefyll yn dweud, 'Mae hon yn broblem i drafnidiaeth', ond beth dŷn ni'n trio cydweithio arno fo ydy, 'Beth ydy'r datrysiadau hynny? Sut ydyn ni'n ei wneud o'n fwy fforddiadwy?' Oherwydd, ar ddiwedd y dydd, os nad ydy pobl yn cael mynediad at chwaraeon a'n gallu cyfranogi, yna maen nhw'n mynd i gostio mwy o arian i'r gwasanaeth iechyd yn y pen draw, boed hynny o ran iechyd meddwl neu iechyd corfforol. Mae'r ochr ataliol yn allweddol bwysig, ond dwi yn cydnabod bod yr heriau hyn yn real ar y funud. Dŷn ni ddim yn mynd i newid hyn dros nos, ond mae'n rhaid inni symud at agenda ataliol yma yng Nghymru, a dyna'r ymrwymiad sydd gan y Llywodraeth hon.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. As I said, these are ongoing conversations. The fact that we have the Deputy First Minister leading on child poverty, the fact that we have Mark Hooper leading on transport, that you have me, and that we also have Nerys Evans, who is looking at the preventative health aspect and public health aspects, all working on this in order to ensure that the plans that we put in place do tackle these challenges, I hope can give you an assurance that we all understand the role that we have to play. I'm not just standing here saying, 'This is a problem for transport', but what we're trying to work together on is the solutions and on how we can make it more affordable. Because, at the end of the day, if people can't access sport and can't participate, then, ultimately, they're going to cost more to the health service, be that because of mental health or physical health. That preventative side is crucially important, but I do recognise that these challenges are very real at present. We're not going to change this overnight, but we do have to move to a preventative agenda here in Wales, and that is this Government's commitment.
