XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
There are some areas of public policy where we can talk comfortably about budgets, targets, frameworks and commissioning arrangements. But end-of-life care is ultimately about something much more fundamental. It's about how we treat another human being when they're at their most vulnerable and how we allow families to spend those final irreplaceable moments together.

For me, this is deeply personal, because I did not get to say goodbye to my father. And anyone who has experienced that will understand that there are some moments in life that simply cannot be recreated later. There is no second opportunity for a final conversation, no second opportunity to hold somebody's hand, no second opportunity to say what you wanted to say. That is why the quality of care in those final days and hours matters not only to the person who is dying, it matters profoundly to those who are left behind. Good palliative care provides dignity to the dying, but it also gives families something extraordinarily important: time, support and the opportunity for closure. We cannot change death, but we can change the experience of dying, and that is why the situation facing hospices across Wales should concern every one of us in this Chamber.

Hospices in Wales support around 20,000 adults and children affected by terminal illness every year. Yet around 70 per cent of the cost of hospice care is funded through charitable donations, and Hospice UK has told us that an estimated 10,000 people in Wales already have unmet palliative care needs—already. Yet demand is projected to increase by a further 21 per cent by 2050, whilst hospices simultaneously face rising staffing, national insurance and operational costs. So, this is not a crisis somewhere over the horizon. There is unmet need today, and we are asking the same services to prepare for substantially greater demand tomorrow.

We are already seeing the consequences. Nearly 30 per cent of Welsh voluntary hospices surveyed are reducing in-patient beds or wider services because of financial and workforce pressures. And this is not an abstract national statistic for those of us in north Wales. At St David's Hospice in Holyhead, a four-bed in-patient unit has been temporarily closed. Four beds might sound insignificant on a Government spreadsheet, but a hospice bed is not simply a number. It may be the place where somebody spends their final night, where a husband says goodbye to his wife, where a daughter holds her father's hand, where a family has one final conversation with somebody they love. So, when we talk about losing four beds, four hospice beds, we are potentially talking about four families losing something they can never get back. And there is another important point here. Allowing hospice provision to deteriorate does not make the need disappear. Community services, hospice services, can support people closer to home, prevent unnecessary hospital admissions and relieve pressure on an NHS already under enormous strain. Fail to fund care properly in one part of the system and the human and financial cost simply appears somewhere else.

The Welsh Government provided £3 million for hospices in 2025-26, and committed to developing a sustainable funding solution. But Hospice UK and Hospices Cymru estimate that £30 million in additional funding is required during the remainder of this Senedd term. So, my question to Government is straightforward: where is the sustainable settlement? Hospices cannot recruit and retain specialist staff on warm words, they cannot keep in-patient beds open with another announcement, and families facing the most difficult days of their lives should not also have to wonder whether the care they desperately need will actually be here.

We spend a great deal of time in this Chamber arguing about priorities. Surely, there can be few greater tests of ours than how we care for people at the end of their lives. For the person dying, it's about dignity. For the family, it's about compassion, the time, the chance to say goodbye. And for those left behind, those final moments can become memories carried for the rest of their lives.

For those reasons, Llywydd, I will be supporting the motion before us today and I urge Members of the Chamber to do the same. I know what it means not to have that goodbye, and that is why I want other families to have the opportunity that I did not, because there are many things that Government can postpone, but a final goodbye is not one of them.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae yna rai meysydd polisi cyhoeddus lle gallwn siarad yn gyfforddus am gyllidebau, targedau, fframweithiau a threfniadau comisiynu. Ond yn y pen draw, mae gofal diwedd oes yn ymwneud â rhywbeth llawer mwy sylfaenol. Mae'n ymwneud â sut rydym yn trin bod dynol arall pan fyddant ar eu mwyaf agored i niwed a sut rydym yn caniatáu i deuluoedd dreulio'r eiliadau olaf hollbwysig hynny gyda'i gilydd.

I mi, mae hyn yn bersonol iawn, oherwydd ni chefais gyfle i ffarwelio â fy nhad. A bydd unrhyw un sydd wedi profi hynny yn deall bod rhai adegau mewn bywyd na ellir eu hail-greu yn ddiweddarach. Nid oes ail gyfle am sgwrs olaf, dim ail gyfle i ddal llaw rhywun, dim ail gyfle i ddweud yr hyn roeddech chi eisiau ei ddweud. Dyna pam y mae ansawdd y gofal yn y dyddiau a'r oriau olaf hynny yn bwysig nid yn unig i'r unigolyn sy'n marw, mae'n eithriadol o bwysig i'r rhai sy'n cael eu gadael ar ôl. Mae gofal lliniarol da yn darparu urddas i'r rhai sy'n marw, ond mae hefyd yn rhoi rhywbeth hynod bwysig i deuluoedd: amser, cefnogaeth a chyfle i ddod â phethau i ben. Ni allwn newid marwolaeth, ond gallwn newid y profiad o farw, a dyna pam y dylai'r sefyllfa sy'n wynebu hosbisau ledled Cymru beri pryder i bob un ohonom yn y Siambr hon.

Mae hosbisau yng Nghymru yn cefnogi tua 20,000 o oedolion a phlant yr effeithir arnynt gan salwch terfynol bob blwyddyn. Ac eto mae tua 70 y cant o gost gofal hosbis yn cael ei ariannu trwy roddion elusennol, ac mae Hospice UK wedi dweud wrthym fod gan oddeutu 10,000 o bobl yng Nghymru eisoes anghenion gofal lliniarol heb eu diwallu—eisoes. Ac eto, rhagwelir y bydd y galw yn cynyddu 21 y cant pellach erbyn 2050, tra bod hosbisau ar yr un pryd yn wynebu costau staffio, yswiriant gwladol a gweithredol cynyddol. Felly, nid argyfwng rywle y tu hwnt i'r gorwel yw hwn. Mae yna angen heb ei ddiwallu heddiw, ac rydym yn gofyn i'r un gwasanaethau baratoi ar gyfer galw llawer mwy yfory.

Rydym eisoes yn gweld y canlyniadau. Mae bron i 30 y cant o hosbisau gwirfoddol Cymru a arolygwyd yn lleihau gwelyau cleifion mewnol neu wasanaethau ehangach oherwydd pwysau ariannol a phwysau gweithlu. Ac nid ystadegau cenedlaethol haniaethol yw’r rhain i ni yng ngogledd Cymru. Yn Hosbis Dewi Sant yng Nghaergybi, mae uned cleifion mewnol pedwar gwely wedi'i chau dros dro. Efallai y bydd pedwar gwely yn swnio'n ddibwys ar daenlen Llywodraeth, ond nid rhif yn unig yw gwely hosbis. Efallai mai dyma lle mae rhywun yn treulio eu noson olaf, lle mae gŵr yn ffarwelio â'i wraig, lle mae merch yn dal llaw ei thad, lle mae teulu'n cael un sgwrs olaf gyda rhywun y maent yn ei garu. Felly, pan siaradwn am golli pedwar gwely, pedwar gwely hosbis, rydym yn sôn o bosibl am bedwar teulu'n colli rhywbeth na allant byth ei gael yn ôl. Ac mae pwynt pwysig arall yma. Nid yw caniatáu i ddarpariaeth hosbis ddirywio yn gwneud i'r angen ddiflannu. Gall gwasanaethau cymunedol, gwasanaethau hosbis, gefnogi pobl yn nes at adref, atal derbyniadau diangen i'r ysbyty a lleddfu pwysau ar y GIG sydd eisoes dan straen enfawr. Os methir ariannu gofal yn iawn mewn un rhan o'r system, bydd y gost ddynol ac ariannol yn ymddangos yn rhywle arall.

Darparodd Llywodraeth Cymru £3 miliwn ar gyfer hosbisau yn 2025-2026, ac ymrwymodd i ddatblygu ateb ariannu cynaliadwy. Ond mae Hospice UK a Hospices Cymru yn amcangyfrif bod angen £30 miliwn o gyllid ychwanegol yn ystod gweddill tymor y Senedd hwn. Felly, mae fy nghwestiwn i'r Llywodraeth yn syml: ble mae'r setliad cynaliadwy? Ni all hosbisau recriwtio a chadw staff arbenigol ar sail geiriau cynnes. Ni allant gadw gwelyau cleifion mewnol ar agor gyda chyhoeddiad arall, ac ni ddylai teuluoedd sy'n wynebu dyddiau anoddaf eu bywydau orfod meddwl tybed a fydd y gofal sydd ei angen arnynt yn ddybryd yma mewn gwirionedd.

Rydym yn treulio llawer iawn o amser yn y Siambr hon yn dadlau am flaenoriaethau. Yn sicr, ni cheir mwy o brawf o'n gwerth na’r ffordd y gofalwn am bobl ar ddiwedd eu hoes. I'r sawl sy'n marw, mae'n ymwneud ag urddas. I'r teulu, mae'n ymwneud â thosturi, yr amser, y cyfle i ffarwelio. Ac i'r rhai sy'n cael eu gadael ar ôl, gall yr adegau olaf hynny ddod yn atgofion a gofiant am weddill eu hoes.

Am y rhesymau hynny, Lywydd, byddaf yn cefnogi'r cynnig sydd ger ein bron heddiw ac rwy'n annog Aelodau'r Siambr i wneud yr un peth. Rwy'n gwybod beth y mae'n ei olygu i beidio â chael y cyfle hwnnw, a dyna pam fy mod am i deuluoedd eraill gael y cyfle na chefais i, oherwydd mae yna lawer o bethau y gall y Llywodraeth eu gohirio, ond nid yw ffarwel olaf yn un ohonynt.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Firstly, can I say 'thank you' to Welsh Labour for bringing forward this debate today? We've already heard how powerfully this issue affects people from across the Chamber. We've heard some incredible stories of people's personal grief and support for this sector, so we're grateful for this debate being here today.

I stand here, Llywydd, also, as one of the many hats that we wear as Members of the Senedd, as the chair of the cross-party group on palliative and hospice care. I want to pay credit to the legend that is Mark Isherwood, who carried that role for a number of years in this place, amongst many roles that he had here. I'm grateful to him for his support throughout his time in this place.

And in that role, I have, of course, also had the privilege of meeting many incredible organisations, in the short time that I've been chairing that cross-party group. Those organisations provide important end-of-life hospice care across Wales, and, as others have, I want to start by thanking them for their incredible work, from the volunteers who man those reception desks in the hospices, right through to those expert clinical staff who are in those hospices day in and day out. I'm also grateful for the support of Jayne Bryant as the vice-chair of that group, and for Elfed Williams as well for his consistency on this, and thank you, Elfed, for sharing your story with us here in this place today.

With the cross-party group, we held an event just a few weeks ago in the Neuadd, Llywydd, and I was grateful to the Cabinet Minister for being able to join us at that event. I know the sector were grateful as well. It was a great opportunity to engage with hospices from across Wales, and I'm sure many of you took the opportunity to do that. I was grateful to be able to spend a few moments with the hospice in my constituency of Fflint Wrecsam, which is Nightingale House Hospice. It's been serving people across Wrexham, Flintshire and east Denbighshire for over 30 years now, and is a shining example of the fantastic work that hospices do in Wales.

I want to remind Members of this place here again today that that cross-party group will meet regularly. I've heard the passionate debate so far in this place and if you want to engage with that cross-party group, please look out for those all-important invites, but I know that we all have very busy diaries to contend with. But let me share with you, as Members, here today that we had a cross-party group meeting just this week and we announced that we're going to undertake an inquiry, as a cross-party group, into community-based palliative care and how that links into hospice care as well. I hope to have some recommendations that the cross-party group can bring to this Senedd as well. And I know that the Cabinet Minister will be interested to see how that may look and how that may shape some of his thinking in the months and years to come as well.

I want to echo the thanks and support already given to those working in this sector and recognise, as others have, the support that's given to around 20,000 children and adults in Wales every year, with that demand growing year in and year out. And we know of the pressure that that good work takes off the NHS, allowing patients to be discharged from hospital and offering 77,000 visits to people in their own homes annually as well.

The point I want to land on, though, Llywydd, is that the one word that comes through to me time and time again from hospices is the word 'certainty'. We hear them desperate for certainty about what their future looks and feels like, and much of that does come down to funding. They need certainty over their budgets, over their funding; they need certainty over what services they can offer; they need certainty over whether Welsh Government will continue to enable them to provide care within our communities. Because if we cannot secure a sustainable funding plan for hospices for the duration of this Senedd term at least, we're at real risk of losing services or whole organisations in our communities, some of which we've already seen the evidence of.

I know the Cabinet Minister may point towards the national commissioning model that is being pulled together, perhaps, at the moment. My understanding is that that's likely to take between five and 10 years to come to fruition. I know the Cabinet Minister led an important debate in this place in January 2024, I believe it was, nearly three years ago, where, as a Chamber, we supported that position as well. But my concern, Cabinet Minister, is the timescale of this. It's nearly three years ago that you led that debate in this place. If that model takes another minimum of five years to develop, that's a long time of uncertainty for this sector. And the plea is that we create that certainty sooner rather than later.

They are of course grateful for those year-by-year allocations that are provided to them; they would not be able to survive without them. But what they do need is long-term, sustainable funding, and a long-term commissioning model to be delivered much sooner than the five to 10 years that perhaps is already being signalled. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn gyntaf, a gaf i ddiolch i Lafur Cymru am gyflwyno'r ddadl hon heddiw? Rydym eisoes wedi clywed pa mor bwerus yw effaith y mater hwn ar bobl ar draws y Siambr. Clywsom straeon anhygoel am alar personol pobl a'u cefnogaeth i'r sector hwn, felly rydym yn ddiolchgar fod y ddadl hon yma heddiw.

Rwy'n sefyll yma hefyd, Lywydd, yn un o'r nifer o hetiau rydym yn eu gwisgo fel Aelodau'r Senedd, fel cadeirydd y grŵp trawsbleidiol ar ofal lliniarol a gofal hosbis, ac rwyf eisiau rhoi clod i’r anhygoel Mark Isherwood a gyflawnodd y rôl honno am nifer o flynyddoedd yn y lle hwn, ymhlith llawer o rolau a oedd ganddo yma. Rwy'n ddiolchgar iddo am ei gefnogaeth drwy gydol ei gyfnod yn y lle hwn.

Ac yn y rôl honno, rwyf innau hefyd wrth gwrs wedi cael y fraint o gyfarfod â llawer o sefydliadau anhygoel yn yr amser byr y bûm yn cadeirio'r grŵp trawsbleidiol hwnnw. Mae'r sefydliadau hynny'n darparu gofal hosbis diwedd oes pwysig ledled Cymru, ac fel y mae eraill wedi'i wneud, rwyf am ddechrau trwy ddiolch iddynt am eu gwaith anhygoel, o'r gwirfoddolwyr sy'n gweithio wrth ddesg y dderbynfa yn yr hosbisau, i’r staff clinigol arbenigol yn yr hosbisau hynny ddydd ar ôl dydd. Rwyf hefyd yn ddiolchgar am gefnogaeth Jane Bryant fel is-gadeirydd y grŵp, ac i Elfed Williams am ei waith cyson ar hyn, a diolch i chi, Elfed, am rannu eich stori gyda ni yma yn y lle hwn heddiw.

A chyda'r grŵp trawsbleidiol, cynhaliwyd digwyddiad ychydig wythnosau yn ôl yn y Neuadd, Lywydd, ac roeddwn yn ddiolchgar i'r Gweinidog Cabinet am allu ymuno â ni yn y digwyddiad hwnnw. Rwy'n gwybod bod y sector yn ddiolchgar hefyd. Roedd yn gyfle gwych i ymgysylltu â hosbisau o bob cwr o Gymru, ac rwy'n siŵr bod llawer ohonoch wedi manteisio ar y cyfle i wneud hynny. Roeddwn yn falch o allu treulio ychydig funudau gyda'r hosbis yn fy etholaeth, Fflint Wrecsam, sef Hosbis Tŷ'r Eos. Mae wedi bod yn gwasanaethu pobl ledled Wrecsam, sir y Fflint, a dwyrain sir Ddinbych ers dros 30 mlynedd bellach, ac mae'n enghraifft ddisglair o'r gwaith gwych y mae hosbisau'n ei wneud yng Nghymru.

Ac rwyf am atgoffa Aelodau'r lle hwn yma eto heddiw y bydd y grŵp trawsbleidiol hwnnw'n cyfarfod yn rheolaidd. Rwyf wedi clywed y ddadl angerddol hyd yn hyn yn y lle hwn ac os ydych chi am ymgysylltu â'r grŵp trawsbleidiol, cadwch lygad am y gwahoddiadau hollbwysig hynny, ond rwy'n gwybod bod gennym ni ddyddiaduron prysur iawn i ymdopi â nhw. Ond gadewch imi rannu yma heddiw gyda chi, fel Aelodau, ein bod ni wedi cael cyfarfod grŵp trawsbleidiol yr wythnos hon ac fe wnaethom gyhoeddi ein bod ni'n mynd i gynnal ymchwiliad, fel grŵp trawsbleidiol, i ofal lliniarol cymunedol a sut y mae hynny'n cysylltu â gofal hosbis yn ogystal. Ac rwy'n gobeithio cael argymhellion y gall y grŵp trawsbleidiol eu cyflwyno i'r Senedd hon. A gwn y bydd gan y Gweinidog Cabinet ddiddordeb mewn gweld sut olwg fydd ar hynny a sut y gallai hynny siapio rhywfaint o'i syniadau yn y misoedd a'r blynyddoedd i ddod.

Rwyf am adleisio'r diolch a'r gefnogaeth a roddwyd eisoes i'r rhai sy'n gweithio yn y sector hwn a chydnabod, fel y gwnaeth eraill, y gefnogaeth a roddir i tua 20,000 o blant ac oedolion yng Nghymru bob blwyddyn, gyda'r galw hwnnw'n tyfu flwyddyn ar ôl blwyddyn. Ac fe wyddom am y pwysau y mae'r gwaith da hwnnw'n ei dynnu oddi ar y GIG, gan ganiatáu i gleifion gael eu rhyddhau o'r ysbyty a chynnig 77,000 o ymweliadau i bobl yn eu cartrefi eu hunain yn flynyddol hefyd.

Y pwynt rwyf am ei grybwyll, serch hynny, Lywydd, yw mai'r un gair sy'n dod drwodd i mi dro ar ôl tro o hosbisau yw'r gair 'sicrwydd'. Rydym yn eu clywed yn awyddus iawn i gael sicrwydd ynghylch eu dyfodol, ac mae llawer o hynny'n dibynnu ar gyllid. Mae angen sicrwydd arnynt ynghylch eu cyllidebau, ynghylch eu cyllid; mae angen sicrwydd arnynt ynghylch pa wasanaethau y gallant eu cynnig; mae angen sicrwydd arnynt y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn parhau i'w galluogi i ddarparu gofal yn ein cymunedau. Oherwydd os na allwn sicrhau cynllun ariannu cynaliadwy ar gyfer hosbisau dros dymor y Senedd hon fan lleiaf, rydym mewn perygl gwirioneddol o golli gwasanaethau neu sefydliadau cyfan yn ein cymunedau, ac rydym eisoes wedi gweld tystiolaeth o rywfaint o hynny.

Rwy'n gwybod bydd y Gweinidog Cabinet yn cyfeirio at y model comisiynu cenedlaethol sy'n cael ei lunio ar hyn o bryd o bosibl. Fy nealltwriaeth i yw bod hwnnw'n debygol o gymryd rhwng pump a 10 mlynedd i ddwyn ffrwyth. Rwy'n gwybod bod y Gweinidog Cabinet wedi arwain dadl bwysig yn y lle hwn ym mis Ionawr 2024, rwy'n credu, bron i dair blynedd yn ôl, lle gwnaethom ni fel Siambr gefnogi'r safbwynt hwnnw hefyd. Ond fy mhryder i, Weinidog Cabinet, yw'r amserlen ar gyfer hyn. Mae bron i dair blynedd er pan y gwnaethoch chi arwain y ddadl honno yn y lle hwn. Os yw'r model hwnnw'n cymryd o leiaf bum mlynedd arall i'w ddatblygu, mae hwnnw'n gyfnod hir o ansicrwydd i'r sector hwn. A'r apêl yw ein bod yn creu'r sicrwydd hwnnw yn gynt yn hytrach nag yn hwyrach.

Wrth gwrs, maent yn ddiolchgar am y dyraniadau blwyddyn ar ôl blwyddyn sy'n cael eu darparu iddynt; ni fyddent yn gallu goroesi hebddynt. Ond yr hyn sydd ei angen arnynt yw cyllid hirdymor, cynaliadwy, a model comisiynu hirdymor i'w gyflwyno'n llawer cynt na'r pum i 10 mlynedd efallai a ragwelir eisoes. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Shwmae, Lywydd; shwmae, bawb. Like my colleagues, I want to firstly start by thanking the staff, the volunteers, the carers, and the families who make palliative and end-of-life care possible across Wales. Now, as someone, like many of you, who would have cared for ageing parents, this debate is really important to me. I've been that family member who has had to sit down with a loved one and explain that there was nothing more that the NHS could do to cure their illness, and that the focus now had to be on keeping them comfortable, pain-free and supported at that time. 

And what our family learned very quickly was just how complex and overwhelming the palliative care system can be to navigate, and particularly when someone is living with multiple conditions and moving between hospital, community and home, and sometimes backwards and forwards. And, in our case, we were dealing with things like stroke, cancer, Parkinson's, motor neurone disease, and so much more, and repeated hospital admissions. And at every single stage, different professionals were then involved, different decisions had to be made, and new information had to be absorbed, and we were constantly paper chasing, trying to make sure we had the right letter and playing catch-up all the time. 

So, for families who are already coping with grief, uncertainty and exhaustion, navigating those systems can really be genuinely daunting. And that experience taught me that palliative care is much more than just medical treatment. It's about communication. It's about co-ordination. And it's also about ensuring that patients and families understand what support is actually available to them—who they can turn to, and what choices are genuinely open to them at that time of need. But most of all, this is about dignity. 

We all recognise the vital contribution that hospices make. They provide specialist care, emotional support, and, of course, practical help to patients and families across Wales. From my perspective, however, this has also got to be a workforce conversation as much as a funding conversation. Every hospice bed, every community visit, and every end-of-life care package depends on people—nurses, healthcare support workers, allied health professionals, social care workers, volunteers and, of course, unpaid carers. So, if we want sustainable palliative care, we need a sustainable workforce. And, as someone with roots in the trade union movement, I want to be clear about something else: caring has got to be valued. It must be valued. Those supporting patients and families at the end of their lives undertake some of the most emotionally demanding work in our society. They deserve secure employment; they deserve fair treatment, fair work, opportunities to develop their skills, and proper support, of course, for their own well-being at that time as well.

But sustainability, of course, is not enough on its own. We've also got to talk about equality and access. We know that not everyone experiences healthcare in the same way. People from black and Asian ethnic minority backgrounds can sometimes face barriers to accessing services. Disabled people may have additional communication, accessibility or support needs. LGBTQ+ people should have confidence that their identities and relationships will be respected. And Welsh language speakers should be able to receive care in the language that feels most natural and, of course, most comforting to them. 

And we must never of course forget unpaid carers who are balancing work, family responsibilities, and often their own health while caring for somebody else that they love. For me, therefore, the test of a successful palliative care system is not simply whether services exist; it's whether the person who needs that care can actually access it, understand it and receive it with dignity, regardless of their background, disability, language, postcode or personal circumstances.

And that brings me back to where I began. Behind every discussion about funding, workforce planning or service provision is a person approaching the end of their life, and a family who are just trying to support them through it. They shouldn't have to spend that precious time struggling to understand a complicated system or worrying about whether the help that they need will be there. Whatever our differences across this Chamber, I hope that we can agree on one fundamental principle: everyone in Wales deserves dignity, they deserve compassion, and they deserve respect at the end of life. All the people, of course, who provide that care, also deserve our support too. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Shwmae, Lywydd; shwmae, bawb. Fel fy nghyd-Aelodau, rwyf am ddechrau yn gyntaf trwy ddiolch i'r staff, y gwirfoddolwyr, y gofalwyr, a'r teuluoedd sy'n gwneud gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes yn bosibl ledled Cymru. Nawr, fel rhywun, fel llawer ohonoch chi, a fyddai wedi gofalu am rieni sy'n heneiddio, mae'r ddadl hon yn bwysig iawn i mi. Rwyf wedi bod yn aelod o'r teulu hwnnw sydd wedi gorfod eistedd gyda rhywun annwyl ac esbonio nad oedd unrhyw beth arall y gallai'r GIG ei wneud i wella eu salwch, a bod yn rhaid i'r ffocws nawr fod ar eu cadw'n gyfforddus, heb boen a chyda chefnogaeth.

A'r hyn a ddysgodd ein teulu ni yn gyflym iawn oedd pa mor gymhleth a llethol y gall y system gofal lliniarol fod i'w llywio, ac yn enwedig pan fydd rhywun yn byw gyda chyflyrau lluosog ac yn symud rhwng ysbyty, cymuned a chartref, ac weithiau yn ôl ac ymlaen. Ac yn ein hachos ni, roeddem yn delio â phethau fel strôc, canser, Parkinson's, clefyd niwronau motor, a llawer mwy, a derbyniadau i'r ysbyty dro ar ôl tro. Ac ar bob cam, roedd gwahanol weithwyr proffesiynol ynghlwm wrth bethau, roedd yn rhaid gwneud penderfyniadau gwahanol, ac roedd yn rhaid amsugno gwybodaeth newydd, ac roeddem yn mynd ar drywydd papur yn barhaol, yn ceisio gwneud yn siŵr bod gennym y llythyr cywir ac yn ceisio dal i fyny drwy'r amser.

Felly, i deuluoedd sydd eisoes yn ymdopi â galar, ansicrwydd a blinder, gall llywio'r systemau hynny fod yn wirioneddol frawychus. Ac mae'r profiad hwnnw wedi dysgu i mi fod gofal lliniarol yn llawer mwy na dim ond triniaeth feddygol. Mae'n ymwneud â chyfathrebu. Mae'n ymwneud â chydlynu. Ac mae hefyd yn ymwneud â sicrhau bod cleifion a theuluoedd yn deall pa gymorth sydd ar gael iddynt mewn gwirionedd—at bwy y gallant droi, a pha ddewisiadau sy'n wirioneddol agored iddynt ar yr adeg honno o angen. Ond yn bennaf oll, mae hyn yn ymwneud ag urddas.

Rydym i gyd yn cydnabod y cyfraniad hanfodol y mae hosbisau'n ei wneud. Maent yn darparu gofal arbenigol, cefnogaeth emosiynol, a chymorth ymarferol wrth gwrs, i gleifion a theuluoedd ledled Cymru. O'm safbwynt i, fodd bynnag, rhaid i hon hefyd fod yn sgwrs am y gweithlu lawn cymaint â sgwrs am ariannu. Mae pob gwely hosbis, pob ymweliad cymunedol, a phob pecyn gofal diwedd oes yn dibynnu ar bobl—nyrsys, gweithwyr cymorth gofal iechyd, gweithwyr proffesiynol perthynol i iechyd, gweithwyr gofal cymdeithasol, gwirfoddolwyr, a gofalwyr di-dâl wrth gwrs. Felly, os ydym eisiau gofal lliniarol cynaliadwy, rydym angen gweithlu cynaliadwy. Ac fel rhywun sydd â gwreiddiau yn y mudiad undebau llafur, rwyf eisiau bod yn glir am rywbeth arall: rhaid inni weld gwerth gofalu. Rhaid gweld ei werth. Mae'r rhai sy'n cefnogi cleifion a theuluoedd ar ddiwedd eu hoes yn gwneud peth o'r gwaith mwyaf emosiynol heriol yn ein cymdeithas. Maent yn haeddu cyflogaeth ddiogel; maent yn haeddu triniaeth deg, gwaith teg, cyfleoedd i ddatblygu eu sgiliau, a chefnogaeth briodol i'w llesiant eu hunain hefyd wrth gwrs.

Ond nid yw cynaliadwyedd yn ddigon ar ei ben ei hun. Rhaid inni siarad hefyd am gydraddoldeb a mynediad. Gwyddom nad yw pawb yn profi gofal iechyd yn yr un modd. Gall pobl o gefndiroedd du, Asiaidd a lleiafrifol ethnig wynebu rhwystrau i fynediad at wasanaethau weithiau. Efallai y bydd gan bobl anabl anghenion cyfathrebu, hygyrchedd neu gymorth ychwanegol. Dylai pobl LHDTC+ fod yn hyderus y bydd eu hunaniaeth a'u perthnasoedd yn cael eu parchu. A dylai siaradwyr Cymraeg allu derbyn gofal yn yr iaith sy'n teimlo'n fwyaf naturiol ac yn fwyaf cysurus iddynt hwy.

Ac ni ddylem byth anghofio gofalwyr di-dâl sy'n cydbwyso cyfrifoldebau gwaith a theulu, a'u hiechyd eu hunain yn aml wrth ofalu am rywun arall y maent yn ei garu. I mi, felly, nid dim ond a yw gwasanaethau'n bodoli yw'r prawf i ddynodi llwyddiant system gofal lliniarol, ond a all yr unigolyn sydd angen y gofal hwnnw gael mynediad ato, a chael ei ddeall a'i dderbyn gydag urddas, beth bynnag y bo'i gefndir, anabledd, iaith, cod post neu amgylchiadau personol.

A daw hynny â mi'n ôl i ble y dechreuais. Y tu ôl i bob trafodaeth am gyllid, cynlluniau gweithlu neu ddarpariaeth gwasanaethau mae unigolyn sy'n agosáu at ddiwedd eu hoes, a theulu sy'n ceisio eu cefnogi drwy'r peth. Ni ddylent orfod treulio'r amser gwerthfawr hwnnw'n brwydro i ddeall system gymhleth neu'n poeni a fydd yr help sydd ei angen arnynt yno ar eu cyfer. Beth bynnag yw ein gwahaniaethau ar draws y Siambr hon, rwy'n gobeithio y gallwn gytuno ar un egwyddor sylfaenol: mae pawb yng Nghymru yn haeddu urddas, maent yn haeddu tosturi, ac maent yn haeddu parch ar ddiwedd eu hoes. Mae'r holl bobl sy'n darparu'r gofal hwnnw hefyd yn haeddu ein cefnogaeth wrth gwrs. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Last night—or last week, rather—I was delighted to visit City Hospice in my constituency. They do fantastic work supporting people with terminal illnesses and their families. They provide care to people within their own homes, helping to keep them connected with their local communities and their support networks for as long as possible, but they also have an amazing drop-in centre in Whitchurch, with beautiful gardens and space for people to take part in meaningful activities, allowing people to keep on living well right to the end of their lives.

They told me about a man they supported who was understandably feeling very low and said that one of the things he was really missing was the opportunity to chat about football, so they created a sports bar where people could drink alcohol-free beer, watch football matches and talk about them, often with a sporting hero as a special guest. I confess that's not something that appeals to me at all personally, but the sports bar has now become one of their most popular activities. This is the real difference that hospices make in people's lives, but this vital work is at risk without sustainable funding and strong collaborative working with local health boards.

The previous Government took steps towards developing a hospice commissioning framework to ensure consistent good practice across Wales. However, I understand there are still significant variations across different areas. The Welsh hospice sector needs an additional £5.5 million of funding this year and an additional £8.2 million of funding in each subsequent year of the Senedd term. This works out at around, as people have said, £30 million for the whole of this Senedd term, which is not a great deal amount of money considering the hugely beneficial impacts for our communities.

On average, Welsh hospices get only around a third of their income from statutory sources and must fundraise for the rest from private donors, which is extremely difficult in the context of the cost-of-living crisis. Any additional financial help for hospices would of course be welcomed, but long-term certainty in both the contracts and grant funding, so that staff and service users can be confident their vital services will be there whenever they are needed. Predictable, multi-year recurring funding allows hospices to better plan ahead and supports their highly skilled staff with a huge number of different medical specialisms embedded within their own local communities.

I'm glad that we all agree that the incredible work of our hospices and palliative care workers is not just worth celebrating in this debate this afternoon, but also worthy of fair and sustainable funding in recognition of their life-affirming work. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Neithiwr—neu yr wythnos diwethaf, yn hytrach—roeddwn yn falch iawn o ymweld â Hosbis y Ddinas yn fy etholaeth. Maent yn gwneud gwaith gwych yn cefnogi pobl â salwch terfynol a'u teuluoedd. Maent yn darparu gofal i bobl yn eu cartrefi eu hunain, gan helpu i'w cadw mewn cysylltiad â'u cymunedau lleol a'u rhwydweithiau cymorth cyhyd â phosibl, ond mae ganddynt hefyd ganolfan galw heibio anhygoel yn yr Eglwys Newydd, gyda gerddi hardd a lle i bobl gymryd rhan mewn gweithgareddau ystyrlon, gan ganiatáu i bobl barhau i fyw'n dda hyd at ddiwedd eu hoes.

Fe wnaethant ddweud wrthyf am ddyn roeddent yn ei gefnogi a oedd, yn ddealladwy, yn teimlo'n isel iawn a dywedodd mai un o'r pethau roedd yn ei golli'n fawr oedd cyfle i sgwrsio am bêl-droed, felly fe wnaethant greu bar chwaraeon lle gallai pobl yfed cwrw di-alcohol, gwylio gemau pêl-droed a siarad amdanynt, yn aml gydag arwr chwaraeon fel gwestai arbennig. Rwy'n cyfaddef nad yw hynny'n rhywbeth sy'n apelio ataf i'n bersonol, ond mae'r bar chwaraeon bellach wedi dod yn un o'u gweithgareddau mwyaf poblogaidd. Dyma'r gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol y mae hosbisau'n ei wneud ym mywydau pobl, ond mae'r gwaith hanfodol hwn yn y fantol heb gyllid cynaliadwy a chydweithio cryf gyda byrddau iechyd lleol.

Rhoddodd y Llywodraeth flaenorol gamau ar waith tuag at ddatblygu fframwaith comisiynu hosbisau i sicrhau ymarfer da cyson ledled Cymru. Fodd bynnag, rwy'n deall bod amrywiadau sylweddol o hyd ar draws gwahanol ardaloedd. Mae angen £5.5 miliwn ychwanegol o gyllid ar sector hosbisau Cymru eleni a £8.2 miliwn ychwanegol o gyllid ym mhob blwyddyn ddilynol o dymor y Senedd. Fel y mae pobl wedi dweud, mae hyn yn golygu tua £30 miliwn i gyd ar gyfer tymor cyfan y Senedd, nad yw'n llawer iawn o arian o ystyried yr effeithiau hynod fuddiol i'n cymunedau.

Ar gyfartaledd, dim ond tua thraean o'u hincwm y mae hosbisau Cymru'n ei gael o ffynonellau statudol a rhaid iddynt godi arian ar gyfer y gweddill gan roddwyr preifat, sy'n hynod o anodd yng nghyd-destun yr argyfwng costau byw. Byddai croeso i unrhyw gymorth ariannol ychwanegol ar gyfer hosbisau wrth gwrs, ond sicrwydd hirdymor hefyd, o ran contractau a chyllid grant, fel y gall staff a defnyddwyr gwasanaeth fod yn hyderus y bydd eu gwasanaethau hanfodol yno pryd bynnag y bydd eu hangen. Mae cyllid aml-flwyddyn rhagweladwy yn caniatáu i hosbisau gynllunio ymlaen llaw yn well ac yn cefnogi eu staff medrus iawn gyda nifer enfawr o wahanol arbenigeddau meddygol wedi'u gwreiddio yn eu cymunedau lleol eu hunain.

Rwy'n falch ein bod ni i gyd yn cytuno bod gwaith anhygoel ein hosbisau a'n gweithwyr gofal lliniarol nid yn unig yn werth ei ddathlu yn y ddadl hon y prynhawn yma, ond hefyd yn deilwng o gyllid teg a chynaliadwy i gydnabod eu gwaith sy'n goleuo bywydau. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Llywydd, and I'd like to thank everyone for sharing their personal stories today. How we care for people in the final chapters of their lives is the ultimate measure of our compassion, our values and our society. Palliative and end-of-life care is not a secondary branch of medicine; it is a fundamental pillar in a truly integrated health and social care system.

In Neath Port Talbot, Marie Curie estimates that 1,550 people would have benefited from palliative and end-of-life care in 2023. In 10 years, they estimate that demand for palliative care in Neath Port Talbot will increase to 1,705 people per year, and what we must remember is that behind every figure, there is a person, there is a family.

Early identification of needs through health boards is vital to inform the planning and delivery of services. I was pleased to see in the Plaid Cymru manifesto commitments to ensure that every regional partnership board includes a palliative and end-of-life care need, because dignity in death should never depend on your postcode.

And we turn to the staff of our hospices across Wales. The support these individuals provide to families could never be measured—the care, experience and compassion enabling people to stay in their homes and communities wherever possible. But an ageing population with increasingly complex conditions means that pressures on our front-line staff will only intensify. If we do not build a resilient community care network, our emergency services will bear the brunt. People who wish to spend their final days in the comfort of their own homes surrounded by their loved ones will continue to be trapped in hospital beds because the community support simply isn't there. I'm glad to see the consensus across the Chamber today to work together to ensure that every individual in Wales can face the end of their life with dignity, comfort and peace.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd, a hoffwn ddiolch i bawb am rannu eu straeon personol heddiw. Y ffordd y gofalwn am bobl y nyddiau olaf eu bywydau yw'r mesur eithaf o'n tosturi, ein gwerthoedd a'n cymdeithas. Nid cangen eilaidd o feddygaeth yw gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes; mae'n biler sylfaenol mewn system iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol wirioneddol integredig.

Yng Nghastell-nedd Port Talbot, mae Marie Curie yn amcangyfrif y byddai 1,550 o bobl wedi elwa o ofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes yn 2023. Ymhen 10 mlynedd, maent yn amcangyfrif y bydd y galw am ofal lliniarol yng Nghastell-nedd Port Talbot yn cynyddu i 1,705 o bobl y flwyddyn, a'r hyn y mae'n rhaid inni gofio yw bod unigolyn, teulu, y tu ôl i bob ffigur.

Mae adnabod anghenion yn gynnar trwy fyrddau iechyd yn hanfodol i lywio'r gwaith o gynllunio a darparu gwasanaethau. Roeddwn i'n falch o weld ymrwymiadau ym maniffesto Plaid Cymru i sicrhau bod pob bwrdd partneriaeth rhanbarthol yn cynnwys angen gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes, oherwydd ni ddylai urddas mewn marwolaeth byth ddibynnu ar eich cod post.

A thrown at staff ein hosbisau ledled Cymru. Nid oes modd mesur y gefnogaeth y mae'r unigolion hyn yn ei ddarparu i deuluoedd—y gofal, y profiad a'r tosturi sy'n galluogi pobl i aros yn eu cartrefi a'u cymunedau lle bynnag y bo modd. Ond mae poblogaeth sy'n heneiddio gyda chyflyrau cynyddol gymhleth yn golygu y bydd pwysau ar ein staff rheng flaen yn dwysáu. Os nad adeiladwn rwydwaith o ofal cymunedol gwydn, ein gwasanaethau argyfwng fydd yn ysgwyddo'r pwysau. Bydd pobl sy'n dymuno treulio eu dyddiau olaf yng nghysur eu cartrefi eu hunain wedi'u hamgylchynu gan eu hanwyliaid yn parhau i fod yn gaeth mewn gwelyau ysbyty am nad yw'r gefnogaeth gymunedol yno. Rwy'n falch o weld consensws ar draws y Siambr heddiw i weithio gyda'n gilydd i sicrhau bod pob unigolyn yng Nghymru yn gallu wynebu diwedd eu hoes gydag urddas, ac mewn cysur a heddwch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I want to start by thanking the Labour group for bringing this motion forward today, and this important debate. Because this is an issue that should unite every single one of us in this Chamber, regardless of our political differences. Like Sam Rowlands, I want to thank Mark Isherwood, who's no longer in this Chamber, for all the work he did in this space. He was a leader in this area for us. We do miss him, but we look forward to seeing what Sam can do in his stead. 

Over the years, I've had the privilege of visiting a number of charities and organisations across Wales that provide care and support for people facing some of the most difficult moments of their lives. I've visited St David's, like Natasha Asghar mentioned. But one particular visit that has stayed with me was a visit to a children's palliative care centre, Tŷ Hafan, close to Cardiff. Seeing the compassion, dedication and extraordinary care provided to children with life-limiting conditions, and support offered not just to the children, but the parents and the families, is something that really does put life in perspective. I want to thank all those people who work in Tŷ Hafan for the amazing work that they do.

But palliative care isn't simply about helping someone at the end of their life, it's about helping people live as well as they possibly can for as long as they possibly can. It's about dignity, comfort, compassion and giving families the opportunity to make precious memories together. I want to pay tribute to every nurse, doctor, healthcare assistant, volunteer and charity worker who makes that possible across our country.

But, Llywydd, behind that incredible work lies a deeply worrying financial reality. Across Wales, hospices support more than 20,000 adults and children every year, yet around two thirds of their income still relies on charitable fundraising. Just last month, Hospice UK and Hospices Cymru warned that an additional £30 million is needed over the remainder of this Senedd term just to protect these essential services. Those are deeply concerning figures for everybody. They're not simply financial pressures on a balance sheet; they have real consequences for patients and families who depend on these services. I welcomed the additional funding that the Welsh Government has provided, including that £4.3 million package announced earlier this year and the work being undertaken to improve how hospices are commissioned, but we must recognise that short-term financial support cannot overtake that long-term security that the service and sector has asked for. We cannot expect our hospices to continue to provide reassurance to families in those most difficult circumstances.

I think there also sits a wider issue of fairness. The Welsh Government itself has acknowledged that around one in four people in Wales currently lack access to hospice care or equivalent specialist palliative care support, and that simply cannot be acceptable. Whether someone lives in Cardiff, the Valleys, rural Powys or north Wales, they should be able to access the same dignity and compassion and that quality of care. We must remember that good palliative care is also about supporting families, providing respite, helping people remain in their own homes and reducing unnecessary pressure on our hospitals. People at the end of their life do not want to end up in accident and emergency departments sat on hard chairs waiting to be seen. That's just not where they want to go.

But I'd just like to say to the new Cabinet Minister: you made a lot of promises to this sector when you were the shadow Minister for this. In January 2024, you led a debate in this Senedd, calling for long-term funding. On 16 July that year, you also said you were unhappy about the delays to the sector. In September, you talked about inefficient progress, and in January and March of this year, you said that funding levels were unsustainable. So, in responding to this debate, Cabinet Minister, I hope that officials haven't got in your ear and changed your mind, because I think some of those assurances that you have given to the sector over the years are going to be held to account. I would like to see that you've listened and are going to act now you're in Government to deliver for this key sector, and deliver for those families and people across Wales who are relying on you to stand up to your promises. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ddechrau drwy ddiolch i'r grŵp Llafur am gyflwyno'r cynnig hwn heddiw, a'r ddadl bwysig hon. Oherwydd mae hwn yn fater a ddylai uno pob un ohonom yn y Siambr hon, beth bynnag yw ein gwahaniaethau gwleidyddol. Fel Sam Rowlands, hoffwn ddiolch i Mark Isherwood, nad yw yn y Siambr hon mwyach, am yr holl waith a wnaeth yn y cyswllt hwn. Roedd yn arweinydd i ni yn y maes hwn. Rydym yn gweld ei golli, ond edrychwn ymlaen at weld beth y gall Sam ei wneud yn ei le.

Dros y blynyddoedd, cefais y fraint o ymweld â nifer o elusennau a sefydliadau ledled Cymru sy'n darparu gofal a chymorth i bobl sy'n wynebu rhai o adegau anoddaf eu bywydau. Rwyf wedi ymweld â Hosbis Dewi Sant, fel y soniodd Natasha Asghar. Ond un ymweliad penodol sydd wedi aros gyda mi oedd ymweliad â chanolfan gofal lliniarol i blant Tŷ Hafan, ger Caerdydd. Mae gweld y tosturi, yr ymroddiad a'r gofal anhygoel a ddarperir i blant â chyflyrau sy'n cyfyngu ar fywyd, a'r gefnogaeth a gynigir nid yn unig i'r plant, ond i'r rhieni a'r teuluoedd, yn rhywbeth sy'n rhoi bywyd mewn persbectif go iawn. Hoffwn ddiolch i'r holl bobl sy'n gweithio yn Tŷ Hafan am y gwaith anhygoel a wnânt.

Ond mae gofal lliniarol yn ymwneud â mwy na helpu rhywun ar ddiwedd eu hoes yn unig, mae'n ymwneud â helpu pobl i fyw cystal ag y gallant cyhyd ag y gallant. Mae'n ymwneud ag urddas, cysur, tosturi a rhoi cyfle i deuluoedd greu atgofion gwerthfawr gyda'i gilydd. Hoffwn dalu teyrnged i bob nyrs, meddyg, cynorthwyydd gofal iechyd, gwirfoddolwr a gweithiwr elusennol sy'n gwneud hynny'n bosibl ledled ein gwlad.

Ond Lywydd, y tu ôl i'r gwaith anhygoel hwnnw, mae realiti ariannol sy'n peri cryn bryder. Ledled Cymru, mae hosbisau'n cefnogi mwy nag 20,000 o oedolion a phlant bob blwyddyn, ond mae oddeutu dwy ran o dair o'u hincwm yn dal i ddibynnu ar godi arian elusennol. Y mis diwethaf, rhybuddiodd Hospice UK a Hospices Cymru fod angen £30 miliwn ychwanegol dros weddill tymor y Senedd hon i ddim ond diogelu'r gwasanaethau hanfodol hyn. Dylai'r ffigurau hynny beri pryder i bawb. Nid pwysau ariannol ar fantolen yn unig mohonynt; mae iddynt ganlyniadau gwirioneddol i gleifion a theuluoedd sy'n dibynnu ar y gwasanaethau hyn. Croesawais y cyllid ychwanegol y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i ddarparu, gan gynnwys y pecyn £4.3 miliwn a gyhoeddwyd yn gynharach eleni a'r gwaith sy'n mynd rhagddo i wella'r ffordd y caiff hosbisau eu comisiynu, ond mae’n rhaid inni gydnabod na all cefnogaeth ariannol tymor byr gymryd lle'r diogelwch hirdymor y mae'r gwasanaeth a'r sector wedi gofyn amdano. Ni allwn ddisgwyl i'n hosbisau barhau i roi sicrwydd i deuluoedd yn yr amgylchiadau anoddaf hynny.

Rwy'n credu bod mater tegwch ehangach yma hefyd. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru ei hun wedi cydnabod nad oes gan oddeutu un o bob pedwar o bobl yng Nghymru fynediad at ofal hosbis neu gymorth gofal lliniarol arbenigol cyfatebol ar hyn o bryd, ac ni all hynny fod yn dderbyniol. P'un a yw rhywun yn byw yng Nghaerdydd, y Cymoedd, cefn gwlad Powys neu ogledd Cymru, dylent allu cael yr un urddas a thosturi a gofal o'r un ansawdd. Rhaid inni gofio bod gofal lliniarol da hefyd yn golygu cefnogi teuluoedd, darparu seibiant, helpu pobl i aros yn eu cartrefi eu hunain a lleihau pwysau diangen ar ein hysbytai. Nid yw pobl ar ddiwedd eu hoes eisiau eistedd ar gadeiriau caled mewn adrannau damweiniau ac achosion brys yn aros i gael eu gweld. Nid dyna lle maent eisiau mynd.

Ond hoffwn ddweud wrth y Gweinidog Cabinet newydd: fe wnaethoch chi lawer o addewidion i'r sector hwn pan oeddech chi'n Weinidog yr wrthblaid ar gyfer hyn. Ym mis Ionawr 2024, fe wnaethoch chi arwain dadl yn y Senedd hon, yn galw am gyllid hirdymor. Ar 16 Gorffennaf y flwyddyn honno, fe ddywedoch chi hefyd eich bod yn anhapus ynghylch yr oedi i'r sector. Ym mis Medi, fe sonioch chi am gynnydd aneffeithlon, ac ym mis Ionawr a mis Mawrth eleni, fe ddywedoch chi fod y lefelau cyllido yn anghynaliadwy. Felly, wrth ymateb i'r ddadl hon, Weinidog Cabinet, rwy'n gobeithio nad yw swyddogion wedi siarad yn eich clust ac wedi newid eich meddwl, gan y credaf y bydd rhywfaint o'r sicrwydd rydych chi wedi'i roi i'r sector dros y blynyddoedd yn cael ei ddwyn i gyfrif. Hoffwn weld eich bod chi wedi gwrando ac yn mynd i weithredu nawr eich bod yn y Llywodraeth i gyflawni ar ran y sector allweddol hwn, a chyflawni ar ran y teuluoedd a'r bobl hynny ledled Cymru sy'n dibynnu arnoch i gadw eich addewidion. Diolch.

Diolch yn fawr iawn, Lywydd, a dwi'n croesawu'r cyfle i ymateb i'r ddadl bwysig hon. Dwi hefyd yn ddiolchgar i Ken Skates am ddod â hi gerbron y Senedd yma heddiw. Hoffwn ddiolch hefyd i'r holl Aelodau am eu cyfraniadau dirdynnol yn ystod y ddadl. Mae hwn yn faes lle mae cryn dipyn o dir cyffredin ar draws y Siambr. Mae llawer yn y cynnig heddiw y gallwn ni gytuno ag o.

Mae gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes o safon uchel yn hynod bwysig. Mae'n golygu bod pobl yn cael eu trin efo urddas, tosturi a gofal. Mae hynny'n bwysig i'r unigolyn. Mae'n bwysig i deuluoedd ac i ofalwyr hefyd, ac mae yr un mor bwysig i'r bobl sy'n eu cefnogi drwy rai o'r adegau mwyaf anodd y byddan nhw byth yn eu hwynebu. Mae hosbisau yn rhan hanfodol o'r gofal hwnnw. Maen nhw'n darparu arbenigedd clinigol gwerthfawr. Maen nhw'n helpu pobl i fyw cystal ag y gallan nhw. Maen nhw'n gweithio law yn llaw efo'r NHS a gwasanaethau cymunedol i ddarparu gofal sy'n dosturiol ac yn canolbwyntio ar yr unigolyn.

Dwi wedi ymweld â nifer o hosbisau fy hun, yn gyntaf fel gwleidydd yr wrthblaid, ac erbyn hyn fel Gweinidog yn y Llywodraeth, a bob tro dwi'n cael fy nharo gan ymroddiad y staff, y gwirfoddolwyr a phawb sy'n rhan o'r gwaith. Dwi'n siŵr fy mod i'n siarad ar ran y Siambr gyfan wrth ddweud bod arnom ni ddyled enfawr o ddiolch iddyn nhw.

Dwi'n deall yn iawn y pryderon sydd wedi codi heddiw am y pwysau sy'n wynebu'r sector, a dwi'n cydymdeimlo'n llwyr gyda nhw. Yn wir, mi oedd llawer o'r materion sydd wedi cael eu hamlygu heddiw yn faterion y gwnes i eu codi fy hun pan oeddwn i ar feinciau'r gwrthbleidiau, fel yr ydyn ni wedi clywed. Mi oedden nhw'n bwysig bryd hynny, ac maen nhw'n parhau yn bwysig heddiw. Mae'r sefyllfa ariannol yn un heriol, a dydw i ddim am esgus fel arall. Mae hosbisau wedi bod yn glir ynglŷn â'r pwysau sy'n wynebu'r sector: costau ynni uwch, cynnydd mewn cyfraniadau yswiriant gwladol, galw cynyddol am wasanaethau ac ansicrwydd ynghylch trefniadau comisiynu.

Mi wnes i glywed y pryderon hynny'n uniongyrchol pan wnes i gyfarfod gyda Hosbisau Cymru yn ddiweddar. Mi wnaethom ni drafod y pwysau sy'n wynebu'r sector ar hyn o bryd. Mi wnaethom ni hefyd drafod y tymor hwy a'r hyn sydd angen ei wneud i roi gwasanaethau hosbis ar sail fwy cynaliadwy.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much, Llywydd, and I welcome the opportunity to respond to this important debate. I'm also grateful to Ken Skates for bringing it before the Senedd today. I'd also like to thank all Members for their poignant contributions during this debate. This is an issue on which there is a great deal of common ground across the Chamber. There is much in today's motion that we could all agree with.

High-quality palliative and end-of-life care is exceptionally important. It means that people are treated with dignity, compassion and care. That's important to the individual. It's important to families and to carers as well, and it is just as important to the people who support them through some of the most difficult times that they will ever face. Hospices are a crucial part of that care. They provide valuable clinical expertise. They help people to live as well as they can. They work hand in hand with the NHS and community services to provide care that is compassionate and focused on the individual.

I have visited a number of hospices myself, first as an opposition politician, and now as a Minister in Government, and on every occasion, I've been struck by the dedication of the staff, the volunteers and everyone else who is part of their work. I'm sure that I speak on behalf of the whole Chamber when I say that we owe a great debt of gratitude to them.

I fully understand the concerns that have been raised today regarding the pressures that face the sector, and I sympathise entirely with them. Indeed, many of the matters that have been highlighted today were matters that I myself raised when I was on the opposition benches, as we have heard. They were important then, and they remain important today. The financial situation is challenging, and I will not pretend otherwise. Hospices have been clear about the pressures that face the sector: higher energy costs, increases in national insurance contributions, increased demand for services, and uncertainty regarding commissioning arrangements.

I heard those concerns directly when I met with Hospices Cymru recently. We discussed the pressures currently facing the sector. We also discussed the longer term and what needs to be done to place hospice services on a more sustainable footing.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
However, recognising the constraints doesn't mean accepting that nothing can be done. There are practical steps that we can and must take to improve services and strengthen planning. Our programme for government contains a clear commitment to address the key challenges facing palliative and end-of-life care. My officials are already working with colleagues across health, social care, regional partnerships and the unpaid carers agenda, to turn that commitment into practical action.

The national service specification supports more consistent planning and delivery. The national competency framework supports workforce development, while the hospice commissioning approach establishes principles for more consistent and sustainable arrangements. The workforce point in the motion is particularly important. The national competency framework provides an important foundation for ensuring staff across health and care have the skills and confidence needed to deliver high-quality palliative and end-of-life care. Palliative care must also be recognised earlier and embedded across the pathways through which people receive care. Through the development of our national cancer strategy and acute and emergency care framework, we are looking at how specialist palliative support can be better integrated across services, supporting earlier access to care, stronger advanced care planning, and more joined-up support for patients and families.

Llywydd, I also want to address the call for fair and sustainable hospice funding. Current arrangements have developed differently across Wales. Hospices have told us that inconsistency and uncertainty make it more difficult to plan services, retain their workforce and invest for the future. Too often, access to palliative and end-of-life care can still be influenced by where people live or how services have developed historically. That variation is not in the interests of patients, families or the wider system. The hospice commissioning guidance gives us a common direction, but its publication was not the end of the process.

The next phase must be about implementation. This includes a national population needs assessment, and work on future commissioning and funding models. The national palliative and end-of-life care programme is working to build a clearer understanding of need across Wales, so that decisions reflect what people require rather than simply reflecting historical patterns of provision. We want to make meaningful progress towards more consistent and sustainable arrangements during this Senedd term. I recognise the sector wants greater certainty and I share that goal. Our focus now is on implementing the commissioning approach and ensuring funding decisions are informed by evidence, agreed service expectations and clearer accountability.

But our attention isn't limited to the longer term. We will continue to pursue practical opportunities to support hospices with immediate pressures, while continuing this wider reform programme. A recent example is the agreement of £800,000 through the all-Wales capital programme to support the redevelopment of City Hospice. Whilst investment in one project can't resolve the pressures facing the sector as a whole, it demonstrates that we are supporting services now while developing more sustainable arrangements for the future. It's also vital that we set a clear, shared policy direction bringing together services, workforce, commissioning, funding, and support for families and carers.

And we're not starting from a blank page, although we recognise there is always room to improve. The quality statement for palliative and end-of-life care, which sets the strategic expectations across health, social care and the third sector, is currently being refreshed and, alongside the existing suite of supporting documents, will help provide the strategic framework for the next phase of improvement.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fodd bynnag, nid yw cydnabod y cyfyngiadau yn golygu derbyn na ellir gwneud unrhyw beth. Mae camau ymarferol y gallwn ac y mae'n rhaid i ni eu cymryd i wella gwasanaethau a chryfhau cynllunio. Mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu'n cynnwys ymrwymiad clir i fynd i'r afael â'r heriau allweddol sy'n wynebu gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes. Mae fy swyddogion eisoes yn gweithio gyda chyd-Aelodau ar draws iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol, partneriaethau rhanbarthol a'r agenda gofalwyr di-dâl i droi'r ymrwymiad hwnnw'n gamau ymarferol.

Mae'r fanyleb gwasanaeth cenedlaethol yn cefnogi cynlluniau a darpariaeth fwy cyson. Mae'r fframwaith cymhwysedd cenedlaethol yn cefnogi'r gwaith o ddatblygu'r gweithlu, tra bo'r dull comisiynu hosbisau'n sefydlu egwyddorion ar gyfer trefniadau mwy cyson a chynaliadwy. Mae'r pwynt ynglŷn â'r gweithlu yn y cynnig yn arbennig o bwysig. Mae'r fframwaith cymhwysedd cenedlaethol yn darparu sylfaen bwysig ar gyfer sicrhau bod gan staff ar draws iechyd a gofal y sgiliau a'r hyder sydd eu hangen i ddarparu gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes o ansawdd uchel. Rhaid cydnabod gofal lliniarol yn gynharach hefyd a'i ymgorffori ar draws y llwybrau y mae pobl yn derbyn gofal drwyddynt. Drwy ddatblygu ein strategaeth canser genedlaethol a'n fframwaith gofal argyfwng ac acíwt, rydym yn edrych ar sut y gellir integreiddio cymorth lliniarol arbenigol yn well ar draws gwasanaethau, gan gefnogi mynediad cynharach at ofal, cynlluniau gofal uwch cryfach, a chymorth mwy cydgysylltiedig i gleifion a theuluoedd.

Lywydd, hoffwn roi sylw hefyd i'r alwad am gyllid teg a chynaliadwy i hosbisau. Mae'r trefniadau presennol wedi datblygu'n wahanol ledled Cymru. Mae hosbisau wedi dweud wrthym fod anghysondeb ac ansicrwydd yn ei gwneud yn anos iddynt gynllunio gwasanaethau, cadw eu gweithlu a buddsoddi ar gyfer y dyfodol. Yn rhy aml, gall mynediad at ofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes ddal i gael ei ddylanwadu gan ble mae pobl yn byw neu'r ffordd y mae gwasanaethau wedi datblygu yn y gorffennol. Nid yw'r amrywiad hwnnw o fudd i gleifion, teuluoedd na'r system ehangach. Mae'r canllawiau comisiynu hosbisau yn rhoi cyfeiriad cyffredin i ni, ond nid eu cyhoeddi oedd diwedd y broses.

Rhaid i'r cam nesaf ymwneud â gweithredu. Mae hyn yn cynnwys asesiad cenedlaethol o anghenion y boblogaeth, a gwaith ar fodelau comisiynu ac ariannu yn y dyfodol. Mae'r rhaglen genedlaethol gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes yn gweithio i feithrin dealltwriaeth gliriach o angen ledled Cymru, fel bod penderfyniadau'n adlewyrchu'r hyn sydd ei angen ar bobl yn hytrach nag adlewyrchu patrymau darpariaeth yn y gorffennol yn unig. Rydym am wneud cynnydd ystyrlon tuag at drefniadau mwy cyson a chynaliadwy yn nhymor y Senedd hon. Rwy'n cydnabod bod y sector eisiau mwy o sicrwydd ac rwy'n rhannu'r nod hwnnw. Ein ffocws nawr yw gweithredu'r dull comisiynu a sicrhau bod penderfyniadau ariannu'n cael eu llywio gan dystiolaeth, disgwyliadau y cytunwyd arnynt gan y gwasanaeth ac atebolrwydd cliriach.

Ond nid yw ein sylw wedi'i gyfyngu i'r tymor hwy. Byddwn yn parhau i fynd ar drywydd cyfleoedd ymarferol i gefnogi hosbisau sy'n wynebu pwysau uniongyrchol, gan barhau â'r rhaglen ddiwygio ehangach hon. Enghraifft ddiweddar yw'r cytundeb o £800,000 drwy'r rhaglen gyfalaf i Gymru gyfan i gefnogi'r gwaith o ailddatblygu Hosbis y Ddinas. Er na all buddsoddi mewn un prosiect ddatrys y pwysau sy'n wynebu'r sector cyfan, mae'n dangos ein bod yn cefnogi gwasanaethau nawr gan ddatblygu trefniadau mwy cynaliadwy ar gyfer y dyfodol. Mae hefyd yn hanfodol ein bod yn gosod cyfeiriad polisi clir ar y cyd, gan ddod â gwasanaethau, y gweithlu, comisiynu, cyllid a chefnogaeth i deuluoedd a gofalwyr at ei gilydd.

Ac nid ydym yn dechrau o dudalen wag, er ein bod yn cydnabod bod lle i wella bob amser. Mae'r datganiad ansawdd ar gyfer gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes, sy'n gosod y disgwyliadau strategol ar draws iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol a'r trydydd sector, yn cael ei adnewyddu ar hyn o bryd, ac ochr yn ochr â'r gyfres bresennol o ddogfennau ategol, fe fydd yn helpu i ddarparu'r fframwaith strategol ar gyfer y cyfnod nesaf o wella.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Ond yn y pen draw, rhaid i fframweithiau cenedlaethol droi'n weithredu ymarferol ar lawr gwlad. Drwy fy sgyrsiau diweddar gyda'r sector, gan gynnwys mewn digwyddiad gan Marie Curie a Hospice UK, dwi wedi clywed y neges yn glir. Mae awydd gwirioneddol i gydweithio, awydd i wella'r gofal a'r cymorth sydd ar gael i bobl wrth iddyn nhw nesáu at ddiwedd eu hoes. Dyna pam dwi wedi gofyn i swyddogion ddechrau'r gwaith o baratoi ar gyfer uwchgynhadledd genedlaethol ar ofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes. Rŷn ni'n bwriadu ei chynnal mis Mawrth nesaf.

Dwi am i'r uwchgynhadledd honno ddod â'r NHS, hosbisau a rhanddeiliad eraill ynghyd. Dwi am iddi helpu i siapio blaenoriaethau'r dyfodol ar gyfer gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes yng Nghymru. Nid y bwriad ydy comisiynu adroddiad arall nac ailadrodd heriau rŷn ni eisoes yn eu deall. Y bwriad ydy dod â phobl at ei gilydd o amgylch rhaglen glir o weithredu a chyflawni yn ystod tymor y Senedd hon.

Lywydd, dydw i ddim yn tanamcangyfrif maint yr heriau sy'n wynebu'r sector. Dwi hefyd yn deall yn iawn y pryder sy'n deillio o'r ansicrwydd ynghylch cyllid a'r gweithlu. Ond, ar yr un pryd, mae'n bwysig cydnabod y cynnydd sydd eisoes wedi bod. Mae'n bwysig hefyd ein bod ni'n manteisio ar y cyfleoedd sydd o'n blaenau ni.

Y tu ôl i bob trafodaeth am gyllid, comisiynu a'r gweithlu, mae pobl go iawn a theuluoedd go iawn—pobl sy'n wynebu rhai o'r amgylchiadau mwyaf anodd y gall unrhyw un ohonon ni ddychmygu. Maen nhw'n haeddu gofal sy'n dosturiol, gofal sydd yn deg, a gofal sydd ar gael pan fo'i angen fwyaf. Mae gennym ni gyfle yn ystod tymor y Senedd yma i wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol trwy gydweithio ar draws yr NHS, hosbisau, llywodraeth leol a'r trydydd sector. Trwy wneud hynny, mi allwn ni greu system sy'n fwy cynaliadwy ac yn fwy cyson—system sy'n rhoi pobl wrth ganol y gofal sy'n cael ei ddarparu.

Dyna'r gwaith rŷn ni wedi ymrwymo iddo fel Llywodraeth, a dyna'r gwaith y byddwn ni'n bwrw ymlaen ag o mewn partneriaeth efo pawb sy'n chwarae rhan mor bwysig wrth ddarparu gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes ledled Cymru. Diolch, Lywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
However, ultimately, national frameworks must become practical action on the ground. Through my recent discussions with the sector, including at an event hosted by Marie Curie and Hospice UK, I have heard a very clear message. There is a genuine appetite for collaboration and an appetite to improve the care and support available to people as they approach the end of their lives. That's why I have asked officials to start the work of preparing for a national summit on palliative and end-of-life care. We intend to hold it next March.

I want that summit to bring together the NHS, hospices and other stakeholders. I want it to help to shape future priorities for palliative and end-of-life care in Wales. The intention is not to commission another report, nor to rehearse the challenges that we already understand. The intention is to bring people together around a clear programme of action and delivery during this Senedd term.

Llywydd, I do not underestimate the scale of the challenges that face the sector. I also understand full well the concerns stemming from uncertainty on funding and the workforce. But, at the same time, it is important to recognise the progress that has already been made. It is also important that we maximise the opportunities ahead of us.

Behind every discussion on funding, commissioning and the workforce are real people and real families—people who face some of the most difficult circumstances that any one of us could imagine. They deserve compassionate care, fair care, and care that is available when it is needed most. We have an opportunity during this Senedd term to make a genuine difference by working together across the NHS, hospices, local government and the third sector. By doing that, we can create a more sustainable and more consistent system—a system that puts people at the heart of the care provided.

That is the task that we have committed to as a Government, and that's the task that we will be taking forward in partnership with everyone who plays such an important part in providing palliative and end-of-life care the length and breadth of Wales. Thank you, Llywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Welsh Labour Debate: Palliative and end-of-life care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Today we do have a cosy consensus. It's one that crosses all parties, and it concerns such a vital area of care that's needed at the end of life and when facing terminal illness. There have been many incredibly valuable contributions, which I have, I'm afraid, too little time available to do justice to. We began with Elfed Williams, who shared his very personal experience of the care provided by hospices and their remarkable staff. He reflected, I think, what many subsequently talked about: just how important it is to give our thanks to the people who make end-of-life experiences and terminal illness manageable.

Benjamin Hodge Mckenna reiterated the pressures facing hospices, outlining the future needs of people with palliative and end-of-life care requirements. Natasha Asghar so rightly identified the compassion and the dignity needed by and provided to children and adults in need of palliative and end-of-life care. St David's hospice in Newport is indeed a remarkable place, and Natasha highlighted workforce issues, including staff well-being. Mike Hedges has long championed the work of hospices and NHS staff, who care for people with terminal illness, and he outlined why high-quality care must be available to people in all parts of Wales. Tŷ Gobaith covers a vast area, and I was told on my visit about the particular challenges of people in remote and rural areas. Mike, along with Rebeca Phillips, rightly called for care not to be subject to a postcode lottery and to ensure equal access for all.

Becca Martin shared what she was told by Mel and presented what I thought was a powerful case, with real emotional depth, for greater support for carers to receive vital respite care. Bereavement support, as Becca outlined, continues through and beyond bereavement, often for many months, potentially even years. Cristiana Emsley also shared a deeply personal experience, reminding us of the need and unmet need across our society. This time last year, Marie Curie nurses provided exceptional end-of-life care for my mum, and she was able to come home to die in dignity and familiar surroundings. I think all of us will know of, or eventually need ourselves, the care of angels at the end of our lives.

Sam Rowlands rightly praised Mark Isherwood for his work in this area, and also Jayne Bryant for her work. And Sam, as chair of the all-party group, I'm sure there's nothing that I can say about this subject that you don't already know, but you were absolutely right to say that certainty of funding is the central ask of hospices. And today I think we heard cross-party support for this to be delivered.

Shav Taj identified how important communication is in finding appropriate care, and Shav was absolutely right to call for fair work, respect, care and support for the workforce. Paul Rock gave us an insight into the operation of hospice sports bars and the way that innovation and person-centred care can enhance palliative and end-of-life experiences. And James Evans shared with us his experience of visiting the phenomenal hospice Tŷ Hafan. He also reiterated the need for funding certainty and fairness of access.

Minister, I believe you gave us assurance, the assurance that we were looking for in this motion, that work will continue and intensify in an area of care so important across political lines and across the communities that we all serve. I'm sure that Members right across this Chamber are keen to help in that work and will scrutinise its progress.

Now, in Government, we increased annual hospice funding and provided extra cost-of-living support to help protect vital services. But unmet and increasing need requires a concerted effort backed by all parties. I fear there will be very few and precious opportunities like this in the coming three and a half years to have consensus and to rally behind an area of delivery that is so important to all. But it is essential that we act collectively and respectfully on such important matters. Care in death is just as important as care at birth. I thank the Minister and all Members who have contributed to this debate, and I hope that we will achieve complete consensus at the vote.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Heddiw, mae gennym gonsensws clir. Mae'n un sy'n croesi pob plaid, ac mae a wnelo â maes gofal mor hanfodol sydd ei angen pan fo rhywun ar ddiwedd eu hoes ac yn wynebu salwch terfynol. Cawsom lawer o gyfraniadau hynod werthfawr, ac mae arnaf ofn nad oes digon o amser gennyf i wneud cyfiawnder â nhw. Fe wnaethom ddechrau gydag Elfed Williams, a rannodd ei brofiad personol iawn o'r gofal a ddarperir gan hosbisau a'u staff rhyfeddol. Rwy'n credu ei fod wedi adlewyrchu'r hyn y siaradodd sawl un amdano wedi hynny: pa mor bwysig yw hi i ddiolch i'r bobl sy'n gwneud profiadau diwedd oes a salwch terfynol yn haws.

Ailadroddodd Benjamin Hodge Mckenna y pwysau y mae hosbisau'n ei wynebu, gan amlinellu anghenion pobl â gofynion gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes yn y dyfodol. Nododd Natasha Asghar, yn gywir ddigon, y tosturi a'r urddas sydd eu hangen ac a ddarperir i blant ac oedolion sydd angen gofal lliniarol a gofal diwedd oes. Mae hosbis Dewi Sant yng Nghasnewydd yn lle anhygoel yn wir, a thynnodd Natasha sylw at faterion yn ymwneud â'r gweithlu, gan gynnwys llesiant staff. Mae Mike Hedges wedi bod yn hyrwyddo gwaith hosbisau a staff y GIG, sy'n gofalu am bobl â salwch terfynol, ers amser maith, ac amlinellodd pam y mae'n rhaid i ofal o ansawdd uchel fod ar gael i bobl ym mhob rhan o Gymru. Mae Tŷ Gobaith yn gwasanaethu ardal eang, a dywedwyd wrthyf ar fy ymweliad am yr heriau penodol sy'n wynebu pobl mewn ardaloedd anghysbell a gwledig. Galwodd Mike, ynghyd â Rebeca Phillips, yn briodol am i ofal beidio â bod yn ddarostyngedig i loteri cod post ac i sicrhau mynediad cyfartal i bawb.

Rhannodd Becca Martin yr hyn a ddywedwyd wrthi gan Mel, a dadleuodd yn bwerus iawn yn fy marn i, gyda dyfnder emosiynol go iawn, dros fwy o gefnogaeth i ofalwyr allu derbyn gofal seibiant hanfodol. Mae cymorth mewn profedigaeth, fel yr amlinellodd Becca, yn parhau drwy gydol profedigaeth a thu hwnt, yn aml am fisoedd lawer, neu flynyddoedd hyd yn oed. Rhannodd Cristiana Emsley brofiad personol iawn hefyd, gan ein hatgoffa o'r angen a'r angen heb ei ddiwallu ar draws ein cymdeithas. Yr adeg hon y llynedd, darparodd nyrsys Marie Curie ofal diwedd oes ardderchog i fy mam fy hun, a bu modd iddi ddod adref i farw mewn urddas ac amgylchedd cyfarwydd. Rwy'n credu y bydd pob un ohonom yn ymwybodol o ofal yr angylion hyn, neu ei angen ein hunain yn y pen draw, ar ddiwedd ein hoes.

Fe wnaeth Sam Rowlands ganmol Mark Isherwood yn gywir ddigon am ei waith yn y maes hwn, a Jayne Bryant hefyd am ei gwaith hithau. A Sam, fel cadeirydd y grŵp trawsbleidiol, rwy'n siŵr nad oes unrhyw beth y gallaf ei ddweud ynglŷn â'r pwnc hwn nad ydych chi'n ei wybod yn barod, ond roeddech yn llygad eich lle'n dweud mai sicrwydd cyllid yw prif gais yr hosbisau. A heddiw, rwy'n credu ein bod wedi clywed cefnogaeth drawsbleidiol i gyflawni hyn.

Nododd Shav Taj pa mor bwysig yw cyfathrebu wrth ddod o hyd i ofal priodol, ac roedd Shav yn llygad ei lle yn galw am waith teg, parch, gofal a chefnogaeth i'r gweithlu. Rhoddodd Paul Rock gipolwg i ni ar weithrediad bariau chwaraeon mewn hosbisau a'r ffordd y gall arloesedd a gofal sy'n canolbwyntio ar yr unigolyn wella profiadau lliniarol a diwedd oes. A rhannodd James Evans ei brofiad o ymweld â hosbis ryfeddol Tŷ Hafan. Ailadroddodd yntau hefyd yr angen am sicrwydd cyllid a thegwch mynediad.

Weinidog, rwy'n credu eich bod wedi rhoi sicrwydd i ni, y sicrwydd roeddem yn chwilio amdano yn y cynnig hwn, y bydd gwaith yn parhau ac yn dwysáu mewn maes gofal mor bwysig ar draws ffiniau gwleidyddol ac ar draws y cymunedau y mae pob un ohonom yn eu gwasanaethu. Rwy'n siŵr bod yr Aelodau ar draws y Siambr hon yn awyddus i helpu yn y gwaith hwnnw ac y byddant yn craffu ar ei gynnydd.

Nawr, yn y Llywodraeth, rydym wedi cynyddu cyllid blynyddol i hosbisau ac wedi darparu cymorth costau byw ychwanegol i helpu i ddiogelu gwasanaethau hanfodol. Ond mae angen ymdrech ar y cyd gyda chefnogaeth pob plaid ar gyfer angen heb ei ddiwallu ac angen sy'n cynyddu. Mae arnaf ofn mai ychydig iawn o gyfleoedd fel hyn a geir dros y tair blynedd a hanner nesaf i sicrhau consensws ac i gefnogi maes cyflawni sydd mor bwysig i bawb. Ond mae'n hanfodol ein bod yn gweithredu ar y cyd ac yn barchus ar faterion mor bwysig. Mae gofal adeg marwolaeth yr un mor bwysig â gofal adeg genedigaeth. Diolch i'r Gweinidog a'r holl Aelodau sydd wedi cyfrannu at y ddadl hon, ac rwy'n gobeithio y cawn gonsensws llwyr yn y bleidlais.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Reform calls for more democratic powers to be put in the hands of local taxpayers. Where Welsh councils propose council tax increases above 4.99 per cent, residents will have the right to approve or reject them through a local referendum. This policy would finally put Welsh taxpayers on an equal footing to their English counterparts. If council leaders want to implement inflation-busting council tax rises year on year, it is only right that they justify it directly to the people who pay—the people who they supposedly work for.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Reform yn galw am roi mwy o bwerau democrataidd yn nwylo trethdalwyr lleol. Lle mae cynghorau Cymru'n cynnig cynnydd uwch na 4.99 y cant yn y dreth gyngor, bydd gan drigolion hawl i’w cymeradwyo neu eu gwrthod drwy refferendwm lleol. Byddai’r polisi hwn yn rhoi trethdalwyr Cymru ar sail gyfartal â threthdalwyr Lloegr o’r diwedd. Os yw arweinwyr cynghorau eisiau cyflwyno cynnydd yn y dreth gyngor sy’n uwch na chwyddiant flwyddyn ar ôl blwyddyn, mae hi ond yn deg eu bod yn cyfiawnhau hynny’n uniongyrchol i’r bobl sy’n talu—y bobl y maent i fod yn gweithio ar eu rhan.
